The signals exhibiting dual orthogonal polarization states can have the same frequency range or different frequency bands. The design has a compact structure by the use of ridged waveguide slot radiators. Advantageously, it can be fed by a waveguide-implemented distribution network mounted to the rear of the antenna to broaden the bandwidth. A dual circularly polarized waveguide slotted array can also be realized by the use of a 3-dB coupler.

articleTitle: Wideband wireless channel predictor relying on environment information
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: With the development of wireless communication system, long-range precise channel prediction is considered to be more important. Traditional predictors require a lot of pilots and their performances degrade very fast after the correlation time, especially in high speed mobile environment. A new parametric channel predictor, CPREI, which is based on the auxiliary environment information, is presented in this paper. This new method can reduce the number of pilots and improve the prediction length. From the evaluation with real measured data, this predictor outperforms the former auto regression (AR) predictor.

Author Keywords: CPREI (Channel Predictor Relying on Rnvironment Information)

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave tunnelling and squeezing effects through 3D coaxial waveguide channel filled with ENZ material
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A three dimensional coaxial metallic waveguide channel filled with ε-near-zero materials is computed using a full wave electromagnetic commercial simulator CST. Simulating predict that electromagnetic waves can be tunnelled and squeezed through the channel, and the incoming TEM wave front is replicated at the output interface, independently of the specific geometry of the channel. A novel ENZ material-related sensor is proposed, and the superior performance of the sensor have been validated.

articleTitle: A new Five-State Markov model for land mobile satellite channels
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new channel model with a five-state Markov chain for land mobile satellite channel (LMSC) is presented. The received amplitude series were classified into three different states according to the degree of shadowing experienced. The two-state model and three-state model are extended to the new five-state model in the paper under the different time-stare of shadowing. The first and second order statistics characters of the model are compared with the measured data and simulation. Finally, the average BER of five-state Markov is compared with six-sate Markov model.

articleTitle: Analysis of electromagnetic interference from pantograph arcing with different trolley locomotive speed in coal mine tunnel
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic interference is very serious in the coal mine tunnel and exhibits quite different characteristics from the ground. This document gives the focus on the pantograph arcing radiation interference generated by the contact line and the trolley locomotive in the coal mine tunnel. Through the theoretical analysis and experiments in Pingdingshan Coal Mine Group, it is said that the more slowly the trolley locomotivepsilas speed the higher the arcing radiation interference. The maximum radiation interference of pantograph arcing is not more than -30 dBmv. The results also show significantly that the wireless communication frequency used in the coal mine is better more than 1900 MHz.

articleTitle: Optimal design of a broadband matching network for an electrically small antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An optimal design approach which combines the real frequency method and the direct numerical optimization is used to design a broadband matching network for an electrically small antenna. According to the characteristic of electrically small antenna, a network topology which improves the electrically small antennapsilas efficiency observably is designed with two methods respectively, and the design result is computed and validated with simulation software. Finally, the two methods are compared in the paper. Results show that the VSWR of the antenna is below 2.5 and its efficiency is above 30% in the pass band by optimal design, that is, the performance of the antenna is improved by a wide margin.

articleTitle: Microwave chaotic Colpitts circuit design
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Chaotic Colpitts oscillating circuit has a broader spectrum characteristic than other chaotic circuits and the complicated bifurcation exhibits rich nonlinear dynamical behaviours. By introducing the normalized state equation, the parameters estimation equation is derived. According to the design requirements of the frequency, the parameter expressions of the main circuit elements are worked out. The simulation results show that the amplitude spectrum of chaotic signal agrees well with the expected frequency distribution; the Colpitts circuit is an excellent tool to generate chaotic signals of high frequency for the broadband communication system.

articleTitle: A modified holographic technique for antenna measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This work describes an extension to the use of indirect holographic techniques for antenna measurements. Previous versions of this work have been restricted to the measurement of high gain antennas without reducing sample spacing and increasing measurement times. This work describes a technique whereby using both sum and difference signals from the complex near field and the reference signal cancellation of the unwanted term in the Fourier domain is achieved enabling measurements to be made on medium gain antennas. Measured results are compared to simulation results for a small pyramidal horn antenna and are shown to provide good agreement.

articleTitle: CPW-fed Band-notched Monopole Antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A printed rectangular monopole antenna fed by a tapered coplanar waveguide (CWP) with a band-notched characteristic is proposed for ultra wideband (UWB) applications. It is shown that the notched or rejected band with a wide operating bandwidth is obtained by embedding an E shape slot in the rectangular radiation patch and its parameters studied in detail. The notched band is controllable by adjusting the lengths and location. With a compact size of 36×34mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, the proposed antenna showing UWB omni-directional radiation patterns that is suitable for UWB applications.

articleTitle: Plane wave synthesis based on the Least Square Method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel method of plane wave synthesis is presented with the application of the least square method in the plane wave synthesis technique. With the rectangular planar array made up of the half-wavelength dipole elements as the theoretical model of plane wave synthesis, the novel method is used to seek optimum amplitude and phase distribution of array element so as to make the uniform degree of the amplitude and phase of quasi-plane wave synthesized to be the best. The calculation results show that the method presented in this paper requires smaller probe array than the traditional methods in order to ensure the quality of quasi-plane wave synthesized, which proves the correctness and validity of the novel method.

articleTitle: Classification for polarimetric SAR images based on subaperture decomposition
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a novel method, which combines subaperture decomposition with H/α/Wishart classifier, is introduced to classify polarimetric synthetic radar (SAR) images. We use H/α plane to initially classify the full-resolution polarimetric SAR image. The initial classification map defines training sets for classification based on coherency matrices of subapertures and wishart distribution. The classified results are then used to define training sets for the next iteration. The convergence of this kind of iteration is much faster than using full-resolution images. And the interpretation of this method is more easily. Results show that the method provides a significant performance improvement with respect to the approaches based on full-resolution images.

articleTitle: Effects of EMP on Bonding Ability of Insulin and its Receptor
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: AIM To discuss the effects of EMP on bonding ability of insulin and itpsilas receptor. METHODS HL-7702[L-02]GNHu6 cells (5times10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup> ldr mL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) were divided into 2 groups: anti-insulin-fluorescent labeling group (including cell-irrad + insulin-irrad group, cell-irrad + normal insulin group, normal cell + insulin-irrad group, normal cell + normal insulin group, total 4 sub-groups) and anti-insulin receptor-fluorescent labeling group (including cell-irrad group, normal cell group, total 2 sub-groups). Some 0.5 mgmiddotmL<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> insulin solution and the groups which need to be irradiated were irradiated by 400 kVmiddotm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> EMP. After the irradiation, the indirect immuno fluorescent experiment was done, immediately. And then, all the samples were detected by FCM. After EMPpsilas irradiation, the percentage of the L-02 cells which were fluorescent-labelled by FITC on cell membranepsilas insulin receptor increased. After EMPpsilas irradiation, the percentage of the L-02 cells which were fluorescent-labelled by FITC on cell membranepsilas insulin increased than un-irradiated, no matter whether the insulin which was put into the L-02 cells was irradiated or not. Compared with the un-irradiated insulin, no matter the irradiated insulin was put into un-irradiated or irradiated L-02 cells, the percentage of the L-02 cells which were fluorescent-labelled by FITC on cell membranepsilas insulin decreased. CONCLUSION 400 k V ldr m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> EMP irradiation may probably change insulinpsilas spatial structure, decrease the bonding ability between insulin and its receptor, and show some excitatory effect on L-02 cells.

articleTitle: Analysis of channel capacities of MIMO systems in an indoor channel environment
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The optimum antenna separation of a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) system for an indoor wireless communication channel is retrieved from average-sense channel capacities which are simulated using a three-dimensional ray-tracing (RT) technique. The RT method is used to simulate the ray paths and path losses of the reflected, transmitted, and diffracted rays in the indoor channel, and consequently compute the channel capacities of the MIMO system for various receiver positions, antenna polarizations, and antenna separations. It is found that the optimum antenna-separation for maximum channel capacity of this channel is 0.333 wavelength.

articleTitle: An estimate method for electromagnetic environment test based on simulation data
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An estimate method based on the result of electromagnetic filed simulation is proposed for practical electromagnetic environment testing. According to the trend of numerical result and the electromagnetic field strength obtained from one test point, electromagnetic field distribution of other places can be computed approximately. The feasibility and accuracy are discussed in this paper. And the impact of the distance between test point and radiation source is also investigated. Though the method proposed is simple to use, it seems attractive for those testers who are willing to improve test efficiency and avoid being hazard by the high power radiation.

articleTitle: Analysis of curved waveguide structures using the MPSTD algorithm
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the multidomain pseudospectral time-domain (MPSTD) algorithm is applied to model the curved waveguide structures. In order to improve the stability of the MPSTD method, the design of a filtering procedure is discussed for corner singularities. By calculating the resonant frequencies and S-parameters of the waveguide structures, numerical results indicate that the MPSTD method can achieve high efficiency and accuracy when use to analyze curved objects. This paper presents a scheme to analyze the waveguide structures, and extends application field of the MPSTD method.

articleTitle: The research of 2-D Multi-Beam cellular networks overlay method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A sort of 2-D Multi-Beam cellular networks overlay method is put forward in this paper. This method aims to make multi-beam distribute in cellular networks by controlling power vectors of the equal arrays, and then attains the purpose of covering both pivot and non-pivot service area with the beams. The design thought of the beams and the calculate method of the power vectors is analyzed, and the imitation result of typical instance indicate that the method is effective.

abstract: Presents the table of contents of the proceedings.

articleTitle: ISAPE2008 The 8th international symposium on antennas, propagation and EM theory proceedings
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: antennas and related topics; propagation and related topics; EM theory and related topics; computational electromagnetics; and electromagnetic compatibility and related topics.

articleTitle: Ionospheric scintillations observed from GPS signals at Guilin in China
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The occurrence of ionospheric scintillations was studied using Global Positioning System (GPS) measurements at Guilin (25.29degN, 110.33degE; geomagnetic: 15.04degN, 181.98 degE). The detailed results are presented for data collected from January 2007 to June 2008. We generally found that amplitude scintillations occurred rarely at night and frequently in the daytime during the period of data analyzed. Strong daytime amplitude scintillations occurred more frequently in 2008 than in 2007. It was found that amplitude scintillation can occur with or without phase scintillation. On the other hand, phase scintillation can occur with or without amplitude scintillation.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of a EMP simulator with absorbing stuff
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, an EMP simulator with absorbing stuff is designed. Firstly, the EMP simulator is analyzed according to the circuit. Secondly, the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method is used to model electromagnetic field of effective work space of the EMP simulator accurately. This work will offer theory direction of simulatorpsilas optimized design.

articleTitle: Exact modeling and fast computation for the radiation characteristics of antenna array-radome structure
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The exact model of an antenna array with a dielectric radome is established by using the surface integral equations and method of moments (SIE-MoM). The proper preconditioning techniques (PT) and the fast multipole method are employed, which obviously improves the property of the MoM matrix equation, reduces the memory occupation and accelerate the iteration convergence of the conjugate gradient (CG) method. Based on the validation of the correctness of the algorithm, some wire antenna arrays with dielectric radomes are numerically simulated, and their radiation characteristics are analyzed.

articleTitle: A new method of electric field intensity calculation on EMI measurements in GTEM cell
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: At present there are several methods to do EMI measurements in GTEM cell, such as EDM, MDM, Linear, Wilsonpsilas method and so on. But the difference between the calculated results of these methods and the EMI results measured in OATS (open area test site) is very large in some situation. This article provides a new method to calculate electric field intensity in GTEM cell using the equivalent dipole of the radiator. And series of experiments were performed to prove the validity and advantage of this method. The experiment results show that the calculated results of new method is more agree with the measured results in OATS, which means that the new method can be considered as a more approached way to calculate the electric field intensity in GTEM cell for EMI measurements.

articleTitle: Unsymmetrical monopole antenna on a T-shaped ground plane
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A compact planar monopole antenna is investigated to cover 870–2450 MHz band. This antennna is an inverted E-shaped monopole with a T-stub ground plane. Influence of asymmetry on bandwidth is discussed. We found that asymmetry can further help improve impedance match with VSWR less than two within the whole desired band.

articleTitle: A multi-layer coupled-line power divider
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, A power divider configuration made of coupled microstrip line is proposed. This power dividing scheme allows a larger range in unequal power dividing ratio and is therefore suitable for array antenna feeds with serially connected elements. The proposed power dividing scheme is also attractive in reducing power loss in the feeding network due to reduced number in power dividers and transmission line lengths. The coupled-line power divider consists of three layers of traces and two slabs of substrates. The top and bottom layers are microstrip lines while the middle layer is the common ground. At the power divider location, elliptical patches present on both the top and bottom layers, and an elliptical aperture is cut on the ground. By adjusting the size of metal patches and the aperture, a controllable power dividing ratio can be achieved.

articleTitle: Conducted pulse measurement based on coaxial pulse probe
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The principle and test method of coaxial pulse probe are discussed in this paper. Coaxial pulse probe, which is composed of a section of hard coaxial cable and electric field sensor embedded in it, is used to measure the waveform of conducted pulse current and voltage. For coaxial pulse probe, because of no magnetic core, the performance of high frequency response and voltage endurance is superior to the common current probe. So coaxial pulse probe is of advantage in conducted pulse measurement. This paper adopts software compensation method in frequency domain to calibrate coaxial pulse probe. The error rate between test results and actual waveform data is less than fifteen percent.

articleTitle: Analysis of the method for EMC radiation safety margin test
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The differences between the direct test method and the indirect test method are found based on the definition of the radiation safety margin in this paper. The mechanisms of the external radiation interference on the system are discussed. A new test method considering the earth line common mode interference and secondary radiation effect is presented. The new test method has high efficiency and low cost. The test results of the new test method are in agreement with the ones of the direct test method.

articleTitle: The technique of dually weighted adaptive nulls-forming in two-dimensional array
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: By analyzing the directional function of a uniform circular array, a kind of dually-weighted signal processing method of two-dimensional null-pointing technique is presented, based on maximum signal-to-noise rule and restricted main lobe qualification. Applied to a uniform two-ring circular array, the result shows that this method is valid in adaptive null-forming in case of multi-interference, and makes the main lobe point to the direction of useful signal.

articleTitle: Automatic amplitude control method of signal generator in electromagnetic sensitivity test
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In electromagnetic sensitivity (EMS) test, the efficiency and veracity of experiments is strongly affected by automatic amplitude control method of signal generator. There are two aspects in those control method. One is the proper set on the initial value of amplitude. The other one is amplitude adjustment method based on initial value. Based on these two aspects, some efficient ways of automatically tuning method of signal generator were summarized in engineer experiments for engineerspsila reference.

articleTitle: A numerical calculation method of substation grounding grids based on a new mathematical model
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on a new mathematical model for electromagnetic fields calculation, a numerical calculation method in design of power substation grounding system is presented. The method is applicable in many cases regardless of frequency. And the method has been proved to be available by calculating cases.

articleTitle: Transmission line method for propagation characteristic of electromagnetic wave in rectangular tunnel
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The paper presents the equivalent transmission line equation which is useful to describe the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves in a tunnel. For the transmission line theory, the mathematical structure of the classical telegrapher equation was preserved, while the coefficients (the per-unit-length parameters) were generalized in order to represent the essential characteristic of the wire structure. At frequencies in the range of 200–4000 MHz transmission takes the form of waveguide propagation in a tunnel, since the wavelengths of the UHF waves are smaller than the tunnel dimensions. So, the tunnel is equivalent to the lossy uniform transmission lines under this condition. In the waveguide structure of the tunnel, the equivalent voltage and current must be introduced, which is called the equivalent transmission line theory. In this paper, the calculation of parameters for many propagation modes in a tunnel is ended to the solution of active equivalent transmission line equation. As examples, the coefficients of equivalent circuit and the attenuation rate for the dominant mode of the vertical polarization electromagnetic wave in the rectangular tunnel are computed. Consistent results with the pattern matching theoretical ones are obtained, and the validity of the presented method is thus verified.

articleTitle: Optimum design of multi-finger SiGe HBT with non-uniform length for power application
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: With a three-dimensional thermal-electrical model, a non-uniform emitter length structure in multi-finger SiGe heterojunction bipolar transistors (HBTs) is presented to improve thermal stability. Compared with the traditional uniform emitter length design, the peak temperature of multi-finger SiGe HBT with non-uniform length is lowered. Therefore, it can operate at large current and has a higher power handling capability in power application.

articleTitle: Microwave permeability and absorbing properties of nano-meter Fe46Co44B10 thin films
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: FeCoB thin films can have high resistivity and relatively high saturation magnetization which are desired for microwave frequency application such as wireless inductors and absorbers. In this study, Fe<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">46</inf>Co<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">44</inf>BB<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> films in thickness of nanometer were deposited on glass substrates by magnetron sputtering method under a uniform applied magnetic field. The as-deposited films exhibit low coercivity of a few Oe, anisotropy field of 50 Oe and 4π Ms of 16.5 kG. Such properties in these films result in a ferromagnetic resonance frequency as high as 2 GHz, a relative permeability μ′ of 350 and a low dissipation μ″ of 50 in the frequency range of 0.05–1 GHz. A resonant absorbing peak locates around 2 GHz which is important to be used as absorbers.

articleTitle: The effects of radar detection in heterogeneous evaporation duct conditions
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on the atmospheric duct experiments in Huang Hai and Bo Hai, this paper introduces the horizontal heterogeneity of the evaporation duct, and studies the effects of radar detection in heterogeneous evaporation duct, concludes that heterogeneous evaporation duct can change the detecting distance of radar and the characteristic of shadow zone in homosphere evaporation duct.

articleTitle: Design of Circularly Polarized Stacked Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A simple technique is developed to improve the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth and quality of circularly polarized stacked microstrip antennas (CPSMAs) using a new C-type single feed. The proposed antenna has been optimized and fabricated, and the computed results agree very well with measurements. The antenna has a 3 dB AR bandwidth of 11.6%, gain is more than 8.2 dBi and the impedance bandwidth for VSWR less than 2 is 29%. The proposed feed optimization technique is useful for rapid design of circular polarized stacked microstrip antennas.

articleTitle: FMCW V-band radar nonlinear analysis and solutions
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The high atmospheric attenuation of V-band millimeter wave, make it only application in outer space and the short-range detection. The FMCW short-range radar systems in this band have more than one non-linear subsystems, some of whom will interfere the system with error, or even wrong. To this end, the first non-linear analysis of the system, focusing on the effect of mixer and VCO on difference frequency signal spectrum, and the interference on ranging. Based on an analysis of the actual collected signal spectrum, use a narrow-band filter to eliminate interference. In the test, the target can be correctly detected out, the difference frequency spectrum is correct, the result meet the design requirements.

articleTitle: Application of patch-removal to spiral antenna backed by mushroom-shaped EBG reflector
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a spiral antenna backed by a mushroom-shaped EBG reflector. The antenna characteristics are investigated on the basis of the electric and magnetic fields obtained by using the finite-difference time-domain method. The investigation reveals that removing some patches from the EBG reflector improves the axial ratio.

articleTitle: Dispersion analysis of capacitive loaded negative-refractive-index transmission lines and associated applications
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Metamaterial or left-handed lines are synthesized by adding a series capacitance and a shunt inductance as loading elements to the host transmission lines. In this paper, we present analysis and design of a left-handed metamaterial line which is loaded with an extra shunt capacitor. Traditional metamaterial lines exhibit an inherent high-pass backward-wave response in their lowest harmonics. The additional shunt loading gives a tighter control on the band-pass response of the periodic structure. Moreover, shunt varactors can be used to tune the frequency response in the desired range. Dispersion properties of the structure are studied and design equations are presented for a generalized capacitive loaded left-handed transmission line structure. A practical compact tunable Wilkinson power divider based on the proposed structure is synthesized and simulation and experimental results are shown.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis of the EBG Structure and Its Application for Low Profile Wire Antennas
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structures are widely used for improving the electromagnetic performance. Its surface wave forbidden frequency band and in-phase reflection frequency band are referred as work frequency band, whose properties are closely associated with the parameters of the EBG structure, such as substrate permittivity, substrate thickness, patch size, gap size, etc. This paper presents a detailed study with method of moment (MoM) on the effect of the parameters, and some EBG design guidelines have been obtained finally. The EBG ground plane application for low profile wire antennas is also investigated in finite element method (FEM). The result indicates that the EBG ground plane greatly improves the work efficiency of the wire antenna in a specific frequency band compared with the ordinary metal ground plane.

articleTitle: Analysis on impulse characteristics of independence grounding devices for lightning protection
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on the circuit theory, this paper adopts the analysis model for the impulse characteristics of grounding device considering the nonlinear soil ionization phenomena in the soil neighbouring the grounding conductors. The impulse characteristics of a typical independence grounding device for lightning protection of electronic and electrical systems inside structures is discussed and the impacts of interval and length of vertical rods, and soil resistivity are also compared by the use of this model. Suggestions for the layout of this grounding device are proposed according to the calculated results.

articleTitle: Miniaturized dual band circularly polarization microstrip antenna for satellite communication
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we proposed microstrip antenna that embedded global star personal mobile satellite communication(receive band : 1.610∼1.6265GHz, transmission band 2.4835∼2.500GHz) terminal. The proposed antenna designed to gain characteristics of circular polarization. Folded structure and plate structure for microstrip were used by changing into 3-dimensional structure. And stacked structure designed to obtain characteristics of dual band circular polarization. Antenna size is length 24mm × width 46mm × height 13mm. The measurement results showed, in the case receive band, −10dB bandwidth is 801VlHz (5%)), the bandwidth below axial ratio 3.5dB is 18MHz, the gain of x-axis pol. is −1.4dB, and HPBW of the E and H plane is 77°, 79°, respectively. In the case of transmission band, −10dB bandwidth is 163MHz(10%), the bandwidth below axial ratio 3.5dB is 20MHz, the gain of x-axis pol. is −1dBd, and HPBW of the E and H plane is 133°, 69°, respectively. Therefore we can confirm that the designed antenna satisfied personal mobile satellite communication terminal.

articleTitle: A hybrid TDIE-PO method for transient analysis of electrically large conducting objects
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An hybrid method based on time domain integral equation (TDIE) coupled with physical optics (PO) is presented for the transient analysis of electrically large conducting objects. The matrix equation of marching-on in time (MOT) procedure is deduced. The numerical results demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the presented method.

articleTitle: Ships imaging based on the fractional autocorrelation
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Due to the noncooperative motions of maneuvering target, as ships, the Doppler shifts of scatterers are usually timev-arying, so that the Range-Doppler algorithm becomes incapable to form synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging. The echo embodying such maneuvering targets is approximated as multi-components chirp signal. Thus, Doppler estimation for multi-components chirp is needed in Range-Instantaneous-Doppler imaging for maneuvering targets. To imaging noncooperative ship target at sea, a new algorithm based on fractional autocorrelation was presented in this paper. The echo from every range cell was correlated by the rotating operator in the time-frequency plane. And the doppler parameters of target were estimated accurately to get fine images, by searching the peak value in the fractional domain. The approach is verified by Radarsat data.

articleTitle: Rectangular helix aperture-coupled wideband microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This novel antenna presented consists of top substrate with a quasi-square patch, middle air gap and bottom substrate with rectangular-helix-slotted ground and open-circuit microstrip feed line(50Ω). It covers 7.9GHZ–9.85GHZ(VSWR≤2, 20.3%). Gain ≥3dB when the ground is large enough. -3dB beam-width is no less than 25° both in E-plane and H-plane. The antenna also has simplicity, compactness, small size, light weight and low profile. So it’s suitable for satellite communication, radio positioning and navigating of micro air vehicle in X-band

articleTitle: Design and realization of signals transform circuit based on CCD devices
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A finite impulse compensation system is designed with charge coupled devices (CCD). The system can compensate the frequency response of various measuring device of network, such as instrument and sensor, etc. so as to extend their work frequency band. The main advantage of the design is its flexibility, the system can be easily changes in the weighting resistances of CCD, provide that the clock frequency can operate the CCD. At the end of this paper, the correctness of design principle has been verified in a simplified experimental condition, and some conclusions are introduced.

articleTitle: A new wideband source number estimation algorithm based on line property
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The research of wideband source number estimation is still key issue in space spectrum estimation. The veracity of the direction finding algorithms is directly influenced by the false alarm and miss probability. However, the performances of them are degraded under the low SNR, colored noise fields and these algorithms have higher computational complexity. To overcome these drawbacks, a new wideband source number estimation algorithm based on line property is proposed. The simulation results with low SNR, colored noise fields demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Techniques for Transient Scattering from Dielectric Bodies
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The time-domain electric, magnetic and combined field integral equations (TDEFIE, TDMFIE and TDCFIE) have been applied widely to the analysis of transient scattering from targets. In this paper, a surface integral equation (TDCFIE) approach is utilized to calculate the transient scattering from arbitrarily shaped, three-dimensional dielectric bodies. In conjunction with the marching-on-in-time method, the TDCFIE-MOT method is used to derive explicit expressions for the present-time current as a function of the incident field and the past history. Sample results showing various geometries are presented and are compared with other numerical techniques. Finally, by an incident Gaussian plane tapered wave, transient scattering from the sea surface developed by Jonswap’s sea spectra is computed.

articleTitle: Design of even-order dual-behavior resonators bandpass filter
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a simple method to design even-order dual-behaviour resonators (DBR) filters is proposed. First, by implementing admittance inverters, the conventional asymmetrical prototype is transformed into a new symmetrical prototype; also, the source and load resistances are equal. Second, a new analytical method for DBR to extract equivalent circuit parameter is proposed. Finally, a bandpass filter with center frequencies of 3.3 GHz is designed, which only consists of series λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>/4 transmission line inverters and DBR based upon parallel different length stubs. The experimental results validate the proposed theory.

articleTitle: Deception Jamming against ISAR with Frequency-Stepped Chirp Signal Based on Time Delay
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: ISAR based on frequency-stepped chirp signal has greater capability of anti-jamming than that of the conventional radar due to its peculiar characteristic. Frequency-stepped chirp signal can achieve total large bandwidth while maintaining narrow instantaneous bandwidth, thus reducing the complexity of radar systems. A new method of jamming the ISAR imaging is proposed, where the received signal is retransmitted after the time delay has been done. Therefore the deception targets can be constructed and the deception jamming against frequency-stepped ISAR is successfully accomplished. Simulations are given to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Portable measuring equipment for extremely low frequency magnetic field shielding effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents the development of a portable measuring equipment for extremely low frequency magnetic field shielding effectiveness. The designs of the current source and antennas are introduced in details. Based on small-loop method, some shielding enclosures are measured. The results indicate that the method is easy and the measuring equipment is highly effective.

articleTitle: Single-layer miniaturized loaded frequency selective surfaces with enhanced bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a novel single-layer miniaturized loaded frequency selective surface (FSS) with enhanced bandwidth operating over the GPS and DCS 1800 frequency band is presented, in which each periodic cell consists of double square loops with different capacitive loadings. To eliminate the undesired coupling between unit cells, the unit cells are placed in the substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity structure. A S-band FSS with such structures is designed, the simulated results show that a band-pass bandwidth of 24.5% (1.49GHz to 1.88GHz) is obtained with an insertion loss of less than 3dB for scan angles up to 45 degree in both TE and TM polarization while the bandwidth of normal loaded FSS is about 3%–5%. Furthermore the FSS dimension is miniaturized to 0.08λ (λ refer to the resonant wavelength).

articleTitle: High-power microwave discharge for producing large-area surface-wave plasmas
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The theory of surface-wave discharge is introduced. A novel structure of the slot antenna array is designed in this paper, and its excitation is numerical analyzed using dipole-antenna array model and FDTD method, respectively. A microwave discharge experiment is operated with this slot-antenna array, and a numerical simulation is also done with FDTD code using the parameter of plasma from experimental measurement. It is found that the designed slot antenna array can excite effectively the microwave coupling into the cavity, and produce the stable large-area high-density plasma.

articleTitle: A Computation of Incoherent Radar Spectra of Anisotropic Temperature Plasma
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The anisotropy of ionosphere plasma is considered in this paper, based on Boltzmannpsilas equation of relaxation collision model. The anisotropic temperature expression was obtained by solving a set of moment equation. Then according to plasma scattering of electromagnetic radiation theory of Sheffield, incoherent scatter spectra are calculated in different directions, the effects of the different electric fields and ratio of electron temperature to ion temperature and the different ion-neutral collision frequency are discussed. It is possible to obtain the reasonable incoherent scatter spectra to consider the ion temperature anisotropic and the change of ion temperature with electric field.

articleTitle: Application of higher order MOM for RCS
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: RCS data is the most important source for SAR processing. For electrically large targets, high accuracy and efficiency calculation is a very difficult topic. Higher order moment method is a Galerkin type version of MOM based on integral equation. It uses entire domain basis function in relatively large patches. Compared with sub-domain basis function, such as RWG, this method can reduce unknowns distinctly. It provides possibilities for electrically large models simulation. This paper adopts bilinear quadrilateral elements as the modelling method and higher order hierarchical polynomial expansion as the basis function. This kind of basis function can use different orders on different elements in order to get the highest efficiency. Based on this theory, codes were made to test its accuracy and efficiency. NASA almond and sphere, two classical metallic RCS test targets, are solved with the codes. Simulation results are identical with the measured and the analytical data.

articleTitle: Simulation on ECM effect based on GMTI using single-antenna SAR
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Study on the electronic countermeasure (ECM) methods and techniques against synthetic aperture radar (SAR) are becoming one of the important topics in the field of electronic warfare (EW). A computer simulation of ECM effect based on Ground Moving Target Indication (GMTI) using single-antenna is proposed in this paper. The model used in the simulation includes real-time active coherent jamming model based on distributed targets, and GMTI model using single-antenna SAR data. Several kinds of the ECM effects in the simulation are emphasized, which include the jamming model’s validity against SAR without GMTI processing, the single-antenna SAR GMTI model’ validity, and the critical condition whether the jamming is effective against the single-antenna SAR-GMTI. The simulation leads to the conclusion that the jamming style is effective not only to SAR without GMTI processing, but also to SAR with GMTI processing.

articleTitle: Earth Equivalent Conductivity Inversion Based on Immune Clonal Computation
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: At present, earth conductivity is a key factor which influences the calculation accuracy of the correction value of low-frequency ground-wave propagation time delay. Based on the practically metrical data and academic estimate method of time delay of low-frequency ground-wave propagation, this paper adopt the immune clonal computation method to inverse the earth equivalent conductivity of the propagation path. Contrast immune monoclonal selection algorithm (IMCSA) and immune polyclonal selection algorithm (IPCSA) with genetic algorithms (GA), the simulation results show that the IPCSA has better stability and higher precision.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation on shielding effectiveness of riveted steel-plate enclosure
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In order to gain shielding enclosure with better shielding effectiveness and lower expense, six riveted steel-plate enclosure models are established. The experimental results show that the shielding effectiveness for continuous wave and transient electromagnetic wave can be above 50 dB if the models are specially designed. Some valuable conclusions for engineering construction are obtained.

articleTitle: Estimate EMS characteristics of electronic system
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: According to describing EMS characteristics of subsystems and components in a complicated Electronic system, this paper put forward a behavioral simulation method to establish EMS characteristics behavioral model of the whole system, then the EMS problems can be analysed and predicted easily. This method discriminates the characteristics of radiation sensitivity/ radiation path from conduction sensitivity/ conduction path. The analysis adopts the antenna feature of the cable and field-cable coupling characteristics. The criterion of the intersystem interference is whether the sensitive system can work normally. So the course to work out EMS characteristics of the whole system can be simplified. The paper puts an abundant practical test data in sensitive analysis, and avoids the larger error problems which come from the numerical equivalent calculation.

articleTitle: The applications of the visual anechoic chamber technique in EMI testing
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The application of the visual anechoic chamber system was discussed. A test was designed to validate the effects of the system used in EMI testing. The results were shown that the average level of the ambient cancelled mode was 11.323 dBmuV / m and the effects were influenced by the distance between the device antenna and the background antenna. The coherence of the two antennas may be another factor. When it comes to the background signals whose amplitudes are near to those of the device signals, the effects will become worse. The source localization mode can distinguish the signals having the same frequency but not coming from the same source. By through the coherence coefficient, the spectrum contents of a device can be received and the leaking area of it can be localized.

articleTitle: Application of scale brass model in EMC design for naval ship
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Scale brass model is viewed as a good method for EMC design and verification. Based on analyzing and researching some literature abroad, a discussion on the use of scale brass models in naval ship is presented, including shipboard antenna design, the antenna placement, prediction of HF electromagnetic environment, RCS, and analysis for transient electromagnetic environment.

articleTitle: Study on the Model for EM Scattering from 2D Target above Sea Surface Based on Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a model building for the EM scattering from simple 2D targets above PM sea surface using the Radial Basis Function (RBF) Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was presented. It is based on the analyses of the basal theory of ANN. The database contains a finite number of samples of EM scattering data obtained with the help of the application of the hybrid method to the composite model. A portion of the database is used to train the network and the rest is used to test the performance of ANN model. This work aims to solve the EM scattering from 2D targets above PM sea surface by using the ANN model.

articleTitle: A new SCS method to improve power combiner efficiency in LINC system
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a new signal component separate (SCS) algorithm named Double Threshold SCS is proposed. It can improve both the efficiency of Chireix-outphasing combiner and the isolated combiner in LINC system. Two thresholds are used to decompose the input signal into two signals with much lower peak-to-average ratio. This method can improve the efficiency of both Chireix-outphasing combiners and isolated combiner without deteriorating the linearity. The result is validated by decomposing a WCDMA downlink signal with 8 dB peak-to-average ratio. Cosimulation in ADS and MATLAB for a complete LINC system is done to support this new algorithm. The simulation results show that the efficiency has been improved tremendously while the linearity is retained the same level as which using the general SCS algorithm.

articleTitle: Research on demand for grounding of shipborne balanced serial communication interface
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Shipborne balanced serial communication interface adopts balanced driving and differential receiving circuit, so its anti-interference ability strengthens. However, ground signal connecting is ignored when forming a balanced serial communication link. This paper analyzes its potential risk of common mode voltage interference and radiation EMI. Furthermore, when reasoning grounding of balanced serial communication interface, we give several measures, such as floating ground and isolated interface, to enhance properties of grounding system for shipborne balanced serial communication interface according to engineering experience.

articleTitle: MLFMA analysis of scattering by conducting objects above a lossy half-space
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic scattering from an arbitrarily shaped 3-D conducting object located above a lossy half space is analyzed using the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). In order to use the MLFMA, a higher order approximation method is used for evaluation of the spatial domain half-space Green’s functions for the far interactions, with the resulting construction applicable to the addition theorem expansion. The porposed method can yield highly accurate results with small group size of the MLFMA and can be easily operated. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A novel direct-conversion structure for non-contact vital sign detection system
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, an analysis on non-contact vital sign detection system is presented. It is concluded that the null point and dc-offset are related, so that the associated problems can be solved. Based on this principle, a novel structure of direct-conversion transceiver, which contains a tuneable phase shifter, is proposed to achieve a better performance. Two sets of simulations are employed to demonstrate the new structure. With this structure, dc-offset and null point can be eliminated and it is very easy to reach the optimal detection.

articleTitle: Quotient-difference algorithm for transient analysis of lossy and dispersive multiconductor transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel approach for transient analysis of coupled transmission line circuits is presented. While frequency domain response is obtained, it must be transformed to time domain response. The 1-domain modified numerical inversion Laplace transform (NILT) and 2-domain modified NILT are utilized for the time domain response. Then quotient-difference algorithm is used to provide higher speed of calculation and precision of results. Both transient responses on the ends of the transmission lines and along the transmission lines are given. The numerical results prove the new approach is efficient and accurate for treating coupled, lossy, nonuniform and dispersive multiconductor transmission line circuits.

articleTitle: An improved spatial impulse-response matrix for error calibration of aperture synthesis radiometers
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The system imperfections have great influence on the performance of aperture synthesis radiometers (ASRs). An improved spatial impulse-response matrix (G matrix) is presented for error calibration of ASRs. Most receiver errors except for the baseline fringe-washing error can be eliminated with the improved G matrix in the image reconstruction of ASR without need for complex hardware calibration system. Simulations show the improved G matrix can improve image quality of inversed image of ASRs. Experiments validate the performance of the improved G matrix.

articleTitle: CPW-fed high-gain micrstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: High gain microstrip antenna using a shorted square wall in the center of the square patch has been reported. In this letter, we presented a modified structure for such a high gain design. Shorting at the center of the patch can be realized by placing number of shorting posts along the radiating edges of the patch, and a CPW-feed structure was used to excite the patch antenna through a slot. It is shown that this configuration exhibit excellent characteristics of return loss and the high-gain. The gain of the antenna was measured to be 10 dBi.

articleTitle: A method for subsurface metallic landmine identification in GPSAR
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A method for subsurface metallic landmine identification in Air- or vehicle-borne Ground Penetrating Synthetic Aperture Radar (GPSAR) using finite difference time domain (FDTD) method combined with genetic algorithm is proposed. To identify the real object, the framework information on landmine is obtained according to the matching algorithm based on number and relative location of one dimensional scattering center. By identifying two kinds of metallic landmines buried beneath a Gaussian rough interface, the effectiveness of the proposed method is testified.

articleTitle: Research of the testing method of radiation pattern for on-board installed antennas
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Test of radiation pattern for on-board installed antennas is a difficult and very necessary. This paper by the testing method is the analysis of mission systems on the basis of actual needs and consideration to facilities, place, and other objective conditions, step by step, level by level test pattern of installed antenna. First, testing pattern of antenna in free-space, and then in the open field in semi-physical tests, the last based on the actual situation in the open field to complete the test of horizontal radiation patterns. From the results of the comparison and analysis, this method can meet the test requirements.

articleTitle: A matrix electrodynamics as an analogue of the Heisenberg’s mechanics
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A matrix approach to solving the electrodynamic problems is suggested. The specificity of one is treatment of an electrodynamic system (ES) as an oscillating system with a finite number of the degrees of freedom. The ES is considered as a set of spatially localized so-called partial oscillators (oscillets). Matrices of unit mutual pseudoenergies and unit mutual energies of the oscillators are evaluated. The eigenfrequencies and the eigenfunctions of the ES can be calculated basing on the lumped elements oscillating system matrix theory. A matrix second-order ordinary differential equation is solved for excited potentials of the ES instead of the DpsilaAlembert equation. The main advantage of the matrix electrodynamics is substitution of the solving the partial derivative differential equations by the less computationally intensive linear algebra problems and the ordinary differential equation integration.

articleTitle: A design of analog predistortion linearizer for RF power amplifier to reduce IMD
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a predistortion linearizer to reducing the third and fifth order intermodulation products in RF power amplifier. Power amplifier linearity has been improved by independently controlling the amplitudes and phases of the third order (IMD3) and fifth order (IMD5) intermodulation distorted products, which are generated by using low frequency second order intermodulation components. Simulation results show that the method is effective and convenient.

articleTitle: Analysis of mutual coupling effect of antenna arrays in direction finding systems
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the method of moment (MoM) technique is used to analyze the actual current distribution in array elements precisely. Then, using mutual impedance network, we can obtain the practical amplitude and phase of the excited voltage in array elements. Consequently, we will analyze the spectrum feature of the arrival signals accurately. And the accuracy and resolution of direction finding system would be improved by correcting the direction finding algorithm with the analysis results. Finally, simulation results with MATLAB are provided to demonstrate mutual coupling effectiveness.

articleTitle: Simulation of electrodynamic phenomena with MEFiSTo-3D NOVA
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A sequence of numerical experiments for illustrating the fundamental behaviour of electromagnetic fields and waves with MEFISTo has been developed. The discussion covers Amperepsilas Circuital Law, wave propagation in free space and in guiding structures, as well as modelling of electromagnetics field with TLM on graphics processing unit.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulink of control system on electromagnetic gear
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic gear is used to transfer power through magnetic field which comes from the electrical coils installed on bearing. The input current may be used to drive the change of the output loads by adjusting on time. This paper has set up the dynamic model of the electromagnetic gear and deduced the transfer function which the electric current is input and the torque is output. According to the principle of the electromagnetic gear transmission system, a pole-zero placement self-tuning control algorithm was designed. At last dynamic Simulink was given. The result shows that the control system of electromagnetic gear transmission can adjust the input electric current to load change in real-time, which makes the dynamic behavior improve greatly.

articleTitle: Investigation on EM scattering by double-layered cylinder alternated between LHM and RHM
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic wave propagation and scattering by the left- and right-handed material cylinder is investigated by incident wave. The schematic geometry of double-layered cylinders alternatively constitutive of left- and right-handed materials is also proposed. Furthermore, the distribution of the electric fields inside and outside the cylinder is calculated by numerical methods. Bizarre EM scattering characteristics of fields affected by introducing the Left-handed material are analyzed on the basis of simulation results. Consequently, the unique property of this medium is further elucidated by analyzing the radar scattering width of cylinder alternately filled with left- and right-handed material.

articleTitle: A new nonlinear circuit model for GaAs Gunn diode in oscillator
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An innovative nonlinear circuit model for Gunn diode in oscillator is introduced based on the physical mechanism of Gunn diode. This model interprets the nonlinear harmonics character of Gunn diode. The simulation prediction and experiment of nonlinear model show feasibility of the nonlinear circuit model for Gunn diode in oscillator.

articleTitle: Full-wave Transient Simulation of Radiation Emission from Power Converter
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a full-wave transient simulation of radiation emission of a power converter by applying CST microwave studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">reg</sup> (CST MWS). IGBT switching spikes, harness and cabling, and all associated passive components are taken into account together with the metallic housing in the simulation. Linear network theory is employed due to the fact that higher harmonic noise is small respect to the operating point. Transient and spectral distribution of electric field within a cubic volume containing the housing is obtained. Shielding net is designed with unit-cell and perturbation methods. The overall emission is successfully reduced with the shielding net.

articleTitle: Analysis of suppressing electromagnetism interference on airborne oil meter
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In the actual project, an airplane oil meter cannot work normally when the radio in the plane is communicating with others. According to the testing results of and the work circumstance of the oil meter, a new method which is based on the characters of waveguide is figured out to suppress the electromagnetic interference.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field of a Vertical Dipole on a Non-perfect Conductor coated with a Negative-index Medium
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The explicit formulas of the electromagnetic field produced by a vertical electric dipole in a negative-index medium coating a non-perfect conductor slab is derived. The contribution of three kinds of wave number to the total field is discussed and investigated. The wave-number of the surface wave is between the wave-number in the air and that in the negative-index media. Because the contribution of each types of wave varies with the medium parameters, the amplitude of total field as function of distance is complicated.

articleTitle: An approach to collector AM bandwidth of Class E power amplifier
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The Class E amplifier’s amplitude modulation mainly relies on the collector DC voltage variations, and the relation between the output signal’s envelop and the modulating signal is linear in theory, but this is actually impossible. Because of the time-variant property of the load network, the analysis of Class E amplifier is somehow difficult. In this paper, a DC analysis model for Collector AM is proposed from a new viewpoint of equivalent average DC response. The main reasons dividing into 4 parts which will cause the distortion of collector AM are analyzed here. After the discussion, the bandwidth of the AM is obtained, and this model is also validated by some simulation results.

articleTitle: Numerical study of 32 element phased array being driven by additional 32 elements antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The paper presents the numerical study of 32-element phased-array antenna with 16-elements beam units along with 16 elements beam steering units. In the subsequent part deals with the working plan related with the radiating units and phase-shifter.

articleTitle: A novel microwave sensor based on rectangular waveguide filled with a DNG material
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel microwave sensor based on rectangular waveguide filled with a double negative (DNG) material is modelled using a full wave electromagnetic commercial simulator CST. Simulating results show that evanescent mode are amplified and transmitted through the structured DNG materials within the frequency band that exhibits negative permittivity and permeability. Evanescent mode is sensitive to permittivity of dielectric material in the detecting zone. Comparing with the conventional microwave resonator, DNG materials-assisted microwave sensor allows for higher sensitivity.

articleTitle: Analysis of image frequency interference in altimeter front-end receiver
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A major problem of the superheterodyne receivers is their response to the undesired frequencies, such as harmonic, image frequency signal. In this paper, special attention is paid to the image frequency interference. In order to analysis the effect of the image frequency signal to the superheterodyne, a behavioural model of a superheterodyne receiver of altimeter is presented and its electromagnetic compatibility is analyzed from the aspects of spectrum and power under the condition of image frequency interference. According to the simulation results, the methods of EMC reinforcement are given. The performance of the improved receiver is simulated and analyzed under the same condition. And the results based on the reinforcement system further verify the effectiveness of the method and the receiver achieves a higher image rejection ration.

articleTitle: Broadband matching network design for antennas using a hybrid genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid genetic algorithm has been successfully applied to broadband matching network design for antennas. Genetic algorithm (GA) and simulated annealing (SA) have been combined to enhance the search efficiency, which can avoid both the slow convergence of GA and the dependence on the initial parameters of SA. Considering the impedance bandwidth and power available from the source delivered to the load, GA based on the parallel selection algorithm is used. The broadband matching network over the band 225 to 400 MHz has been designed based on this improved hybrid genetic algorithm. The results show that the broadband matching network has broad impedance bandwidth and high covering power. The improved hybrid GA is an effective method of the broadband antenna matching network design.

articleTitle: The negative refraction between two-dimensional unloaded and loaded transmission line media
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A two-dimensional scalar wave equation for a general two-dimensional distributed network is established. Voltage distribution, current distribution, impedance expressions in x-direction and z-direction, and propagation constant for the twodimension loaded L, C transmission line media (negative-refractive-index media) and the unloaded transmission line media (positive-refractive-index media) are presented. These derived expressions are used in design of both the electrical parameters for these two media and proper excitation for plane wave. Plane voltage wave incident at an angle of 60° on the interface between the positive-refractive-index media and negative-refractive-index media for a relative refractive index of −√3 are simulated by microwave circuit. The simulation results show that the negative refraction happens at the interface, which verify the derived formulas in this paper.

articleTitle: PEG algorithm based interleavers design for systematic IRA codes
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Irregular-repeat-accumulate (IRA) codes are random-like codes having extremely good performance over AWGN channel. They can be viewed as special kinds of LDPC codes in the way their parity-check matrix are sparse. Like LDPC codes, they can be decoded using the messages-passing algorithm efficiently, while the existence of short length circles in their corresponding factor graph representation has a deleterious effect on the BER performance of the codes. Progressive edge-growth (PEG) algorithm is a famous method to construct factor graph without short circles. In this paper, we use PEG algorithm to construct the parity-check matrix of IRA codes firstly, and then deduce the interleaver design of the codes. Experimental results show significant improvement on the BER performance of the IRA codes with designed interleaver over the IRA codes with randomly choose interleaver.

articleTitle: Layer-oriented Integration Vector Element of Multilayer RAM
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In electromagnetic scattering solution of multilayer radar absorbing material (RAM), RAM is divided into multilayer thin elements under precise requirement, but quantity of elements grows too excessive to solve. In order to reduce solution scale, we develop layer-oriented integration arithmetic, and apply it into curve quadrilateral vector element. The core of this arithmetic is monolayer integral strategy of multilayer elements. In this paper, we solve electromagnetic scattering of multilayer RAM with layer-oriented integration vector element for presenting the arithmetic process. Numerical examples show that the layer-oriented integration vector element is high precise and applicable for multilayer thin structures electromagnetic computation.

articleTitle: Path holding probability based ad hoc cross-layer routing method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper is based on the stability and proposing an Ad Hoc cross-layer routing method based on path holding probability. According to the distance between nodes, it can alter the transmit power and decrease the power of source node efficiently. According to the simulation, the routing stability can be ensured when two nodespsila distance is changing, and the power can be saved.

articleTitle: Analysis of performance before and after GNSS antenna is installed on the airplane
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Satellite navigation antenna, which is frequently used, often takes the form of microstrip. Because of its high sensitivity, its characteristics are easily affected by the outside environment. Whether the work environment of satellite navigation antenna is good or not exerts a direct influence upon its performance. This paper explores the work environment of satellite antenna, namely, factors to influent the function of GNSS (global navigation satellite system) and further studies on the electromagnetic compatibility of GNSS. It is supposed that this paper can be helpful to the design of EMC of the entire aircraft.

articleTitle: Dual-Frequency Circularly Polarized Annular-Ring Slot Antenna Fed by a Double-Bent Microstripline
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel design of a dual-frequency circularly polarized annular ring slot antenna is presented. The dual-frequency characteristic is achieved using a single-layer double-bent microstripline-fed configuration coupled to a dual-annular ring slot antenna. The 10 dB return loss impedance bandwidths (VSWRles2) for the lower and higher band are 31.3% and 10.6%, respectively. The 3 dB axial-ratio bandwidths are 10.5% and 1.5% with respect to 2.15 GHz and 3.8 GHz, respectively. The proposed antenna with broad axial-ratio bandwidth at the lower frequency and simple structure is easy to be fabricated and adjusted.

articleTitle: Atomic Force Microscope Observation on CHO Cell Membrane after Electromagnetic Pulses Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Atomic force microscope (AFM) has been used to visualize the morphological change on the surface of CHO cell membrane before and after Electromagnetic pulses (EMP)irradiation. The results showed that there were different sizes and shapes of membrane perforate (the width is 0.66-0.39 um, the depth is 392.95 nm) after 400 kV/m 200 pulses EMP irradiation. The numbers of cell membrane perforates were decreased with EMP field intensity and the pulses numbers decreasing. It is suggested that EMP irradiation can cause the membrane perforate of CHO cell directly. The numbers of cell membrane perforates were increased with EMP field intensity and the pulses numbers increasing. EMP induced membrane perforate may play a very important role in EMP bio-effects.

articleTitle: Radar cross-section enhancement of concrete specimen with trihedral corner reflector structure buried
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Low electromagnetic fields backscattering from concrete pavement as its smooth surface results the much darker image feature when exposures to imaging radar when compared with rough surface such as vegetation. In this paper, exploratory research on radar cross-section enhancement of concrete specimens with trihedral corner reflectors structure buried is presented. Scattering properties of concrete specimen, corner reflector and concrete specimen mixed with corner reflectors are numerical simulation based on the model of finite difference-time domain(FD-TD) in lossy dielectric with perfect matched layer(PML) in z-direction and period boundary conditions(PBC) in x, y-direction. In the conditions of given incident wave and dielectric coefficient of concrete specimen, the monostatic RCS of concrete specimen mixed trihedral corner reflectors with 5 times of wavelength is 3.6 dBsm, the average is -9.8 dBsm in direction of 30-60 degree.

articleTitle: A miniature broadband semi-circular fed patch antenna on a small-size ground plane
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A double layer patch antenna for wideband and small size is proposed. By introducing a long U-shaped notch and semi-circular feeding, a wide bandwidth of 62% for the return loss (S11) ≪ −10 have been achieved. Besides, the ground plane size of the proposed antenna is relatively small compared with other patch antenna.

articleTitle: Experiment on terahertz imaging with an NbN SIS detector
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A simple imaging system operating at 0.5 THz band, utilizing nearly quantum-limited sensitive NbN superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) mixers, is demonstrated. The system is proved to have a spatial resolution of 2.7 mm and sensitivity of 1.6 K with a 100 mm diameter collecting Teflon lens. The results show that this imaging modality is applicable to diverse areas in active or passive mode.

articleTitle: Research on the anti-interference of radiation of the elevator on the spot
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: the elevator experimental platform and simulated EMI signal system were built to test anti-interference of radiation on the spot. The destination was to find the frequency ranges and electric field intension which made the elevator lose its functions. The influence of shielding and ground connection would be researched as well. All the malfunctions would be summarized during the whole experiment. And the reasons of those malfunctions should be found. Some measures were taken to avoid the malfunctions under the electromagnetic interference signals. All the whole experiment provides new ways to keep the safe motion of the elevator equipment in public occasions

articleTitle: Two-dimensional Clustering-based Discriminant Analysis for SAR ATR
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper gives a new image feature extraction technique coined two-dimensional clustering-based discriminant analysis (2DCDA), which is based on 2D image matrices for constructing the scatter matrices and assumes that the data obeys the multimodal distribution. The detailed procedure of 2DCDA is to first partition each class of the data into multiple clusters via fast 2D global k-means clustering algorithm, and then try to find some directions such that the projections of every pair of clusters from different classes are well separated while the within-cluster scatter is minimized. Therefore, it fully exploits the cluster information and alleviates the linearly unseparable problem to some extent.
