According to the projection fashion, we divide 2DCDA into two versions, the right 2DCDA (R-2DCDA) and the left 2DCDA (L-2DCDA). They compress the image row or column only, so they need more features. To solve this problem, two-directional 2DCDA ((2D)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>CDA) is developed, which compresses the image row and column simultaneously. Experiments have been carried out for recognition of three types of ground vehicles in the Moving and Stationary Target Acquisition and Recognition (MSTAR) public database to evaluate and compare the performances of the proposed algorithms with other methods. Results demonstrate that 2DCDA and (2D)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>CDA are effective. And, the highest recognition rate is up to 97.89%, which is the best ever reported in the literatures.

articleTitle: The lightning radiation electromagnetic field data acquisition system based on virtual instrument
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The lightning radiation electromagnetic field data acquisition system is developed based on virtual instrument, which is used to acquire the lightning electromagnetic radiation data. The hardware is mainly composed of GPS receiver, PXI6608 Counter/Timer and PX5105 Data Acquisition Card made by America NI Company, as well as the lightning detection stations. Virtual instrument is controlled by using the software programmed by Virtual Instrument. By utilizing storage procedures, the lightning electromagnetic signals which are received by 5105 are stored. The 6608 Counter/Timer acquires time from GPS receiver and generates pulse at certain time. Thus the lightning electromagnetic signals can be timed. The accuracy of the system is conformed by experiments.

articleTitle: Antenna, feeding and adjusting network for TD-SCDMA base station
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A collinear planar dipole antenna array, with its feeding and adjusting network, is designed, realized and tested. The antenna element comprises nine planar dipoles, fed by coaxial lines which were connected to a nine-way power divider. For each antenna element, measured SWR is less than 1.5 over the TD-SCDMA frequency band (1880-1920, 2010-2025 MHz); the 3 dB beam width is over 90deg in H-plane and more than 7deg in E-plane; the gain varies from 15.2 dB to 16.1 dB, satisfying the industry standard. Six antenna elements compose a larger array. A ldquo6+1rdquo adjusting board, used to get the signals in both transmit and receive mode for power adjusting, is also designed. The coupling factors between adjusting port and each elementpsilas port are about -26 dB, with a maximum variation of 0.7 dB.

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: Automatic frequency detection circuit for first intermediate frequency of DRM/DAB receivers
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents skills to reduce the detection time and assure the frequency grid of the automatic frequency detector circuit in a DRM/DAB receiver. To support minimum receiver requirements for DRM “Draft Version 1.21”, we introduce an automatic frequency detector (AFD) technique for the low-IF receiver, which uses a new detect algorithm to improve detector speed. The simulation results show that the detect time and the frequency grid meet the requirements of DRM “Draft Version 1.21”. The AFD circuit is designed with SMIC 0.18 μm RF CMOS process. Post-simulation results show that the minimum detection time is 1.748 ms. It consumes 0.64 mW under a 1.8 V supply. The core area is 0.15×0.18 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: A Simulation of The Electromagnetic Pulse Coupling with The Planar Inverted F Antenna (PIFA) Inside A Mobile Handset
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Here, the process is simulated by using the finite-difference time-domain method when the electromagnetic pulse is coupled with the planar inverted F antenna in a mobile handset box. By the analysis for the intensity and energy of the electric field, the coupling characteristic is presented. It is concluded that the peak value of the electromagnetic pulse in the model box is very large and the power density is very strong. So it will bring some obvious effects on the mobile handset. It is also tested that the analysis method is helpful to understand the electromagnetic compatibility of a mobile antenna.

articleTitle: A New Variable-Step-Size LMS Adaptive Filtering Algorithm and Its Application in Adaptive Noise Jamming Cancellation System
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new variable-step-size LMS algorithm is proposed, and it performance is analyzed. Simulation results indicate that the performance is superior to that of existing VSS algorithm and NLMS algorithm. The proposed algorithm is then applied to adaptive noise jamming cancellation system; the computer simulation shows superior performance over the NLMS algorithm and MVSS algorithm.

articleTitle: A new FDTD algorithm for plasma at high collision frequencies
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new JEC finite-different time-domain algorithm for plasma at high collision frequencies is derived using the time piecewise linear extrapolation for electric field and the recursive convolution relationship between the current density and the electric field (JEC). A simple approach for error analysis is presented to compare the errors of the new method and some other existing methods. The results show that the original JEC method is only suitable for plasma with low collision frequencies, and the new method can greatly improve the accuracy over the original JEC method while maintain relative high computational efficiency. The high accuracy of the new method and the effectiveness of error analysis are also confirmed by computing the interaction of electromagnetic waves with a one-dimension plasma slab.

articleTitle: Effects of electromagnetic pulse on the tight junction of mice blood-testis-barrier
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: AIM. To investigate the changes of the mice testes and the tight junction (Tj) relative molecular and to identify the molecular mechanisms of the mice blood-testis-barrier (BTB) permea- bility increasing after the mice were exposed to electromagnetic pulse (EMP). METHODS. Observe the changes vimentin of the mice testes by laser scanning confocal technique. RESULTS. After the 200 kVm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> EMP (the accumulative pulse times was 200) exposure, the vimentin in sustentacular cells of testis became irregularly shortened and derangement, and the intensity of immuno- fluorescence also showed ununiformity compared with control. CONCLUSION. The increasing of mice BTB permeability perhaps caused by the changing of vimentin.

articleTitle: An efficient algorithm for electromagnetic scattering analysis using curve RWG basis function and adaptively modified characteristic basis function method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid method of curve RWG basis function (CRWG) and adaptively modified characteristic basis function method (AMCBFM) is proposed for the method-of-moments (MoM) solution of integral equations for three-dimensional (3-D) electromagnetic (EM) problems. Numerical results show that the CRWG-AMCBFM solves the real problems accurately and can save more RAM storage and CPU time than conventional methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of statistic model of digital radiometer detector
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The digital radiometer detector (DRD) is a digital signal processing detector, of which the essential elements hardware consist of a high-speed, high-resolution analog-to digital converter (ADC). A practical ADC will have an uneven step size (differential nonlinearity) between quantization thresholds, and changes the probability distribution of the sampled data and further distorts the input signal, statistics models may also be limited by deterministic interference coming from local oscillator (LO) leakage. This paper is to implement a high speed data acquisition instrument that can record the digital data stream in real time, develops an approach using high-order moment to measure kurtosis of the signal of DRD.

articleTitle: Study on Ship-Formation Detection by Missile-Borne Radar using DBS Imaging Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: For moving ship-formation target, problems such as the appearance of virtual targets occurs if general DBS procedure was adopted for detection. This paper improves DBS realization method accordingly: to estimate the whole velocity of ship-formation target first, and then carve up azimuth direction Doppler basing on both this velocity and the velocity of the missile. Researches are made of ship target models, and the results prove the effectiveness of procedure.

articleTitle: Study on scintillation of radio wave propagation through the ionospheric irregularities
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The Parabolic equation which the radio wave propagation through the ionospheric irregularities was established in this paper. The Rytov and Markov approximation method was used to solve it. Derived the scintillation index of radio wave through the ionosphere. And the results was analyzed by used the power-law spectrum. The result shows that the high or low of the radio frequency, the thickness of the electron density irregularity, the inner and the outer scale, the spectral index and the variance of the fluctuation of the electron density are all have a effect on the scintillation index of radio wave .final, the theoretical results of the scintillation index were compared with the experimental one .

articleTitle: Efficient and accurate signal transient and crosstalk noise determination of frequency-variant RLC transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new signal transient and crosstalk noise determination method of frequency-variant RLC transmission lines is presented. In order to investigate the realistic transmission line characteristics, two coupled lines are experimentally characterized by using s-parameters up to 20GHz. Then the signal transients and crosstalk noises are directly determined with the measured s-parameters and compared with conventional SPICE simulation results. Thereby, it is shown that the conventional approach may lead to significant design error. In contrast, the proposed method is very accurate as well as efficient.

articleTitle: Investigation on the near-field computational model of frequency-scan antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on the structure and characteristics of the frequency-scan antenna, the near-field computational model is constructed. The array elementpsilas phases are presented firstly and the radiation power of each array element is speculated according to the antenna aperture distribution. On the basis of the phase and power, the equation of radiation fields of each array element is obtained. According to the superposition principle, the near-field radiation model of frequency-scan array antenna is achieved. By the near-field model the near field distributions, pattern, and beam width are computed, which are consistent with the test data and prove the modelpsilas correctness.

articleTitle: Dual-band stacked microstrip antenna using a parabolic-pedestal
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: To improve the characteristics of the dual-band stacked microstrip antenna, a novel antenna configuration with parabolic-pedestal is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna is to be used in a mobile satellite communications system. The key parameters of the proposed antenna are analyzed. Simulation results demonstrated that the proposed antenna not only works well at dual-band with circular polarization(CP), but also acts higher gain at low elevation angle.

articleTitle: Perfect imaging using negative-refractive-index transmission-line slab with a source in it
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: under the fully matched condition, we present microwave-circuit simulation results of subwavelength imaging by a slab composed of L, C loaded transmission-line media with a source in it., and we have found that, although the single-interface lens composed of an negative refractive index medium and a positive refractive index medium are not involved in the growth of evanescent wave to achieve perfect imaging, such a slab with a source in it leads to growing evanescent voltage wave away from the source in the slab, thus enhancing the resolution of the images.

articleTitle: Time-reversed electromagnetic wave propagation in case of directional antennas
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we study the influence of directional antennas on the propagation of time reversal (TR) ultra wideband (UWB) electromagnetic waves in a typical indoor environment. The directional antennas are formed by a dipole and a reflection horn with different flare directions. The results demonstrate that the directional antennas can influence the time and spatial focusing characteristics of the TR UWB electromagnetic waves. It implies that the UWB communication performance can be improved by using directional antennas.

articleTitle: Crosstalk analysis and suppression in high-frequency handset terminal device PCB design
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Crosstalk is analyzed in Printed Circuit Board design. The damage of the crosstalk to the system is summed up and the relevant factors effecting crosstalk are studied. Using these characteristics such as small size, high frequency and big density in high-frequency handset terminal, Y-wiring topology is designed. It guarantees effectively signal terminal resistance matching in each SDRAM. At the same time there is the same loop area in the handset terminal. Many suppressive measures are used in the process of wiring, for example it needs series end match to electrical length trace and capacitive / high inductive load trace. Signal line which has stronger signal is added protection line at both ends of it. Clock and signal line meet the 3-W principles. These measures improve the system’s ability to suppression crosstalk allowing the system to meet the requirements of Electro Magnetic Interference.

articleTitle: Effect of optical transmitter on EMP plane wave distribution
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: When electric field is measured, one kind of optical fiber measurement system is often used. And we are often concerned with the effect of the device on electromagnetic wave distribution. in this paper, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is used to model the effect of optical transmitter on EMP (electromagnetic pulse) plane wave distribution. From the numerical result, we find the law of the effect of optical transmitter on EMP plane wave distribution.

articleTitle: Conducted interference simulation analyse of High-power Switching Power Supply (SPS)
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper introduces the principle of EMI for high-power switching power supply and analyzes the coupling path of conducted interference. The models of circuit simulating are established by PSpice software. The analysis of simulating result and testing data are helpful for the design of switching power supplypsilas electromagnetic compatibility.

articleTitle: Resonant frequency and sensitivity analysis of Hilbert curve fractal antennas for DRM communications
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the resonant frequency and sensitivity characteristics of Hilbert curve fractal antennas is presented. Several fractal-shaped Hilbert monopoles have been constructed, based on theoretical calculation, EM simulation and measurement. The formulation on resonant frequency of the Hilbert antennas is derived and verified. Experimental results show that compared with the receiving antenna for DRM (Digital Radio Mondiale) system provided by a professional company, our receiving antenna has a high enough receiving sensitivity but a reduced size.

articleTitle: FDTD analysis for radiated performance of a cylinder plasma antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: To analyze a dielectric medium encapsulation, round cylinder monopole plasma antenna which is more practicable and applicable, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is implemented. Influences of operating frequency and dielectric tube permittivity on the far-field antenna radiation intensity are investigated and evaluated. Numerical results indicate that the radiated power plays as a function of the dielectric constant of outside tube. Optimal value combination of several parameters should be concerned for attaining the most powerful radiated performance.

articleTitle: Target identification and signal processing of millimeter-wave active/passive detecting system based on TMS320LF2812
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper conducts the research to the 3 mm wave band millimeter-wave active passive compound detection system signal examination and processing, major study on the design and methods of the system based on TMS320LF2812 signal processor, including the signal analysis and processing of millimeter-wave radar and radiometer. Some practical ways has been improved on hardware and software in AD sampling, and has been confirmed the validity of the proposed scheme by experiment.

articleTitle: Measurements of 50-meter radio telescope antenna using satellite beacons and solar noise
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Basic specifications are introduced simply for 50-meter radio telescope antenna in this paper. Measurement principle and method of gain and pattern for 50-meter radio telescope antenna are described using solar noise and satellite beacon signal. Finally, measurement results of 50-meter antenna gain and pattern are given, and measuring results meet prediction requirements.

articleTitle: Numerical modelling and FDTD analysis of electromagnetic fields radiated by surge in coal mine
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Such reasons as the start-stop or short circuit fault of high power equipment, the operation of power supply equipment, the frequency conversion equipment and the fault of power supply network will lead to surge. Surge injected into transmission lines will produce intense transient radiated electromagnetic field, which can severely interfere in normal operation of electronic systems around and even damage them. In this paper, radiated electromagnetic field by surge injecting into transmission line is studied using FDTD method as dipole radiator and the numerical model is established. It calculated the radiated electromagnetic field at the different position in a rectangular coal tunnel. All results presented help the application and designing of surge protection for electronic device and the arrangement of electronic device and wire cable.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Adaptive Bit Loading for SFBC-OFDM over WSSUS Multipath Channels
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper studies an adaptive modulation technique combined with space-frequency block coded OFDM (SFBC-OFDM) over wide sense stationary uncorrelated scattering (WSSUS) multipath channels. Chow’s adaptive bit loading algorithm and Alamouti’s diversity scheme are employed in the two transmitter antennas and two receiver antennas SFBC-OFDM. WSSUS multipath channels are discussed. Then scattering function is presented. Simulation results show that adaptive SFBC-OFDM has 1.5 dB advantage compared with fixed modulation SFBC-OFDM. Furthermore, adaptive SFBC-OFDM requires less additional power gain than fixed modulation SFBC-OFDM, which can combat feedback in WSSUS multipath channel.

articleTitle: Scattering Center Estimation of UWB Radar Target with Improved MP Method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Successful target discrimination using the ultra wideband (UWB) radar hinges on an accurate understanding of the scattering behavior of complex radar targets. In the present study, a mathematical model of the UWB radar target is developed based on the analysis of its impulse response. Then an improved matrix pencil (MP) method with adaptive selection of the frequency sampling interval is employed to extract the target scattering centers. Simulation experiments show that with the proposed method, the estimated scattering centers of the given UWB radar target are accurate and reliable even at the low signal noise ratio of 6dB.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler Extraction of Frequency-Stepped Chirp Signal Based on the Hough Transform
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The micro-Doppler (m-D) effect induced by the rotating parts in a radar target or mechanical vibrations of the target body provides a new approach for auto target recognition. In this paper, the m-D effect in frequency-stepped chirp signal is analyzed. Compared with that in the traditional chirp signal, the m-D effect in frequency-stepped chirp signal appears some new characteristics. To extract these m-D characteristics and so to obtain the micro-motion information of the target for auto recognition, the extended Hough Transform is applied into detecting the parameters of the curves on the range-slow time plane after the analytical expressions of the curves deduced. Computer simulations have proved the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of the bounded-wave EMP simulator
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a bounded-wave EMP simulator is introduced. The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is used to model electromagnetic field at working region produced by the bounded-wave EMP simulator accurately. And this numerical analysis method is feasible from the compare of numerical result with experiment result.

articleTitle: MPIE-MOM analysis of the horizontal LPDA array over ground plane
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, Mixed Potential Electric Integral Equation (MPIE) and the method of moments (MOM) are used to analyze the horizontal log-periodic dipole antenna (LPDA) array over ground plane. The microwave network theory is applied to deal with the excitation. The direct discrete complex image method (DCIM) and a quick way are applied to calculate the Sommerfeld integral in the near and far region respectively. At last, we get the direction graphs of the antenna, which is rather satisfied.

articleTitle: The overview of dynamic frequency spectrum access based on some advanced techniques
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The paper introduced the present insufficient situation of the frequency spectrum resource. Several effective techniques to raise the utilization efficiency of the spectrum and corresponding developments of their applications, such as the Cognitive Radios, the Ultra-Wide Band radio, the Water Filling Principle and the Detection & Avoidance Mechanism, are analyzed and compared, which are increasingly significant to the spectrum regulation and management research.

articleTitle: Design of low cost 33° base station antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Current wireless communication market has a demand for high performance and low cost 33° base station antenna. In this paper the design topology of a low cost 33° base station antenna is presented. The frequency band is 1710–2170MHz. The single antenna element used in the antenna array is an aperture-coupled cross polarized patch antenna. The antenna array has a 3-column staggering structure with 30 elements in total. With a novel design of feeding network, a high performance and low cost 33° base station antenna was successfully developed.

articleTitle: On the evaluation of TL mode currents along transmission lines of finite length
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we derive a general equation describing the TL (transmission line) mode currents at any position along a uniform two-wire transmission line and give the solution expression excited by an incident plane wave. We also simplify the expressions for the per unit length distributed parameters and point out the application conditions. The derived equations are tested against numerical results obtained using the electromagnetic field analysis software FEKO, and reasonably good agreements are found. And the simplified expressions for the per unit length distributed parameters also perform well.

articleTitle: Interference analysis of UWB to the satellite communication services
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: UWB communication system operates by transmitting signals over a very wide band in spectrum, so there must be a coexistence problem between UWB and the other radio services. In order to investigate the interference to the narrowband wireless services from the UWB devices, a novel three-dimensional projection interference model has been presented. This analysis model is fit for analyzing the interfered equipments which have high gain and sharp-cut directional character by making the projection and the directional weight for UWB distributing. Based on the proposed model, the interference from UWB equipments to the satellite communication services has been analyzed and the limitations on the UWB transmit power in C-band has been regulated by simulation.

articleTitle: Magnetic sensor based on giant magnetoimpedance effect
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A giant magnetoimpedance (GMI) magnetic sensor is designed in the present work. Differing from the previously reported sensors, a couple of permanent magnets are applied to provide a bias magnetic field for the sensor probe which consists of commercial amorphous ribbon. A negative feedback-coil is adopted to improve the linearity of the sensor output. The sensor shows sensitivity of 1041 mV/Oe in the range of plusmn1 Oe, measurement precision of less than 0.11% at room temperature and good thermal stability in the temperature region between -20 and 30degC.

articleTitle: Research on electromagnetic environmental measurement system based on GIS and GPIB technology
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper elaborates the electromagnetic environmental measurement system’s principle of design, analyzes the software frame and the hardware design characteristics of electromagnetic environmental measurement system based on the GIS (geographic information system) and the GPS localization module, designs the mobile electromagnetic environmental measurement system in the virtual instrument’s foundation. In addition, it proposes a new electromagnetic environmental measurement stationing method.

articleTitle: Analysis of scattering by combined conducting and dielectric objects using multi-region time domain integral equation scheme
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Multi-region time domain integral equation is developed to analyze the electromagnetic scattering from three dimensional combined conducting and dielectric objects. In this paper, we use EFIE-PMCHM to solve the time domain integral equations. The problem is formulated in terms of a set of coupled integral equations involving equivalent electric and magnetic surface currents based on equivalence theorem. The conducting structures and the dielectric materials are modeled by planar triangular patches, RWG basis and Galerkin method are used. Numerical results are given for various structures and compared with other available data. The numerical results show that the present method has satisfying accuracy.

articleTitle: Array calibration for radar low-angle tracking based on electromagnetic matched field processing
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The essence of the radar low-angle tracking is to estimate accurately the height of a specified target in the presence of complicated propagation conditions, including specular multipath propagation, diffuse reflection, diffraction propagation, range-dependent atmosphere refractivity stratification and other anomalous propagations conditions (e.g., ducting). An effective array data model for low-angle tracking is the prerequisite to many model-based low-angle tracking algorithm. The commonly-used planewave arrival data model usually can not take into account much aforementioned anomalous propagation in radar low-angle tracking, which results in serve performance deterioration in the practical low-angle tracking scenario. In light of the electromagnetic matched field processing (EM-MFP), an effective method of array calibration is proposed in this paper, in which the numerical solution of the parabolic wave equation (PWE) at sensor locations in 3D space is substituted for the traditional plane-wave arrival data model. The biggest advantage to using the PWE method is that it gives a full-wave solution for the field in the presence of range-dependent environments, and almost all aforementioned anomalous propagations conditions can be taken into account automatically. For demonstration, comparisons of the array data for a classic low-angle tracking scenario are presented between the traditional planewave arrival data model and the proposed PWE data model.

articleTitle: Analysis of EM Scattering from Electrically Large Target over 2-D Sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The mechanism of composite scattering from complex electrically large target over the two-dimensional (2-D) randomly rough sea surface is researched based on the modified ldquofour-path modelrdquo. Kirchhoff approximation and the method of equivalent edge currents are applied to analyze the backscattering of the sea model generated with the Monte Carlo method and the electrically large target respectively. The issue of the coupling field between the target and the sea surface is solved with the principle of image. A model of the composite scattering from the complex target over the sea surface is proposed to analyze the affects of sea background to the scattering characteristics of the target. The EM scattering characteristics of the electrically large target in the sea clutter background is discussed with the numerical results.

articleTitle: Geometrically based statistical model for multipath propagation of satellite to the earth channel in urban environment
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a statistical geometric model for multipath propagation of the satellite communication, which provides some insight into the spatial properties of wideband channels. The Closed-form explicit expressions of the probability density functions (pdf) of the time of arrival (TOA) for multipath signals and the power delay profile according to the various elevation angles of the satellite are derived, where the scatterers are located uniformly within a three-dimensional (3-D) hemisphere around the receiver. The proposed model provides the general and accurate theoretical approximations for multipath propagation channels, which is validated by the simulation. The result shows that the numerical outcomes from the model are consistent with the measurements, especially effective in urban environment, and is thus useful for analytical purposes.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation on the coupling rules of PCB based on the ESD immunity test platform
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on an ESD immunity test platform defined by IEC61000-4-2 and with the contact discharge, the peaks of coupling voltage and current, which induced in a printed circuit board (PCB), were measured at different discharge voltages. Through the data these rules were found, they are: the peaks of coupling voltage(U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>) and current(I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>) are linear to the discharge voltage(U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">esd</inf>) in the range of −0.3KV∼−4.2KVand 0.3KV∼4.2KV, that is: U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>=a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">esd</inf>+b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>; I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>=a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">esd</inf>+b<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. In addition, the trend line of Up and the output impedance of a coupled circuit in the PCB under test were provided in this paper.

articleTitle: Tunable defect states of ferromagnetic electromagnetic band gap materials
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper has studied the transmission properties of two-dimensional ferrite electromagnetic band gap materials with linear defect under a mutative static applied magnetic field by the multiple-scattering method and experiments. We find that the defect states of magnetized 2D ferrite electromagnetic band gap structures can be tuned by the applied static magnetic field for the radiations in transverse magnetic mode.

articleTitle: Acoustic damping of a four-clamped membrane in ultrasonic microdevice
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we present an analytical model of the acoustic damping of a four-clamped membrane in a ultrasonic microelectromechanical system device. The model is used to analyze effects of acoustic damping on the dynamic behavior of the microdevice, in which four-clamped membranes vibrate at ultrasonic frequency, as well as a flow goes through the cavity under the membrane. A modified Reynolds equation that is derived from the Navier-Stokes equation is used to model the flow under the membrane. The analytical solutions for the damping pressure and force are obtained. Factors that affect the damping pressure and force are discussed. Furthermore, the result of the microdevice’s performance form analytical calculation is compared with that from the finite element method in ANSYS.

articleTitle: Design of band-pass Filters at Ka-band with waveguide- to microstrip- transition
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A rectangular waveguide e-plane fin-line filters compared with metal insert filters at Ka-band is introduced. Optimized design dates for four- to five-resonator type filters are given for mid-band frequency of about 35.6 GHz. Emulational passband insertion losses of prototypes are 0.02dB and 0.5dB respectively. A type of waveguide- to microstrip- transition on a single dielectric substrate for millimeter wave band-pass filters is proposed. The insertion losses of the two filters connected with transition are 0.5dB and 0.9dB respectively, which satisfy engineering.

articleTitle: Dual-feed circular polarization folded microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the dual-feed circular polarization folded microstrip antenna for GPS(Global Position System) is being suggested as a developed antenna which could have a broader 3dB beam width of axial ratio than planar type such as microstrip patch antennas. Furthermore, a proposed antenna has several advantages which are appropriate for edge of blade on plane or miniaturized portable receiver. The results in this study obtained MB beam width of axial ratio, which is wider than regular planar type patch GPS antennas. The maximum gain for the x axis parallel polarization was −2.9dBi, and the y axis was −1.1dBi. An average value of axial ratio is 2.68dB, when the frequency was at 1.575GHz, from 0° to 180° at 30° intervals in zx-plane.

articleTitle: Design of Depressed-ridge waveguide by finite element method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Transmission characteristics of Depressed-ridge waveguide are analyzed by the finite element method. Design data of cutoff wavelength of the dominant mode and single-mode bandwidth for different ridge dimensions are presented in tabulated forms. Field patterns of the dominant mode and the first higher-order TE mode are also illustrated. Numerical results are obtained, which are useful in the design of many microwave components and subsystems.

articleTitle: Time-domain detection with blind separation of unknown source signals
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper a new technique is proposed for time-domain detection in energy detection. The proposed scheme is based on a independent-component analysis (ICA): blind separation of unknown source signals. This method not only improves the nicety of time-domain detection for narrow band signal and the sinusoidal signal but also reduces the power of the whole detection system.

articleTitle: Refractive index in a metamaterial cloak
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Rigorous analysis on the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves in a metamaterial cloak is presented. Fresnel's equation of wave normals is successfully derived from Maxwell's equation by studying the characteristics of a monochromatic plane wave propagated in a metamaterial cloak.

articleTitle: Analysis of transient grounding resistance under pulsed discharging current with parallel FDTD algorithm
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents numerical analysis to the transient grounding resistance of grounding conductor under pulsed discharging current using parallel FDTD algorithm based on domain decomposition method and MPI library. It is found that the adopted parallel strategy is feasible by comparing the result of serial FDTD computing with the proposed method. The parallel FDTD algorithm provides an efficient method for analysing a large-scale grounding system or dealing with fine structure of grounding conductor, which often lead to huge computation requirement.

articleTitle: On the Interference between DS-UWB Systems
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The coexistence of UWB communication systems may cause interference. In this paper, the interference between two DS-UWB asynchronous communication systems is studied. Theoretical analysis and numerical simulations indicate that strong interference occurs as the chip rate increases, and the low date-rate DS-UWB system suffers more form the high-rate system. By properly increasing the length of pseudo noise (PN) codes, the anti-jamming performance of DS-UWB system can be improved significantly.

articleTitle: The design of diversity receiving in Rerverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the diversity techniques in Rerverberation Chamber is firstly presented. With the introduction of space diversity, by using multi-receiving antenna, we can get more effective signals and greatly reduce the variance. Through comparing the results of non-diversity with the ones of diversity, it is tested that diversity techniques can improve the signal variance of Rerverberation Chamber.

articleTitle: Miniaturized electromagnetic band-gap structure to suppress simultaneous switching noise
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we present a method to miniaturize electromagnetic band-gap (EBG) structure. EBG is used to suppress noise occurred as tons of switching devices switch on and off simultaneously. In the proposed model, slits exist on both power and ground planes of power distribution network (PDN), which is called 3-D EBG due to the geometric configuration. The method to miniaturize EBG structure is based on signal return path theorem. Two-layered 3-D EBG structure is fabricated, and 3-D full-wave simulator, HFSS, is used to calculate S21 parameter. The measured and calculated S21 parameter shows high isolation, suppressing the noise under −40dB at the frequency range of 2.8 GHz to 8.3 GHz. Finally the performance of the proposed 3-D EBG structure is compared with the other two 2-D EBG structures and shows its superiority to them.

articleTitle: Symbol LU Method of Large Scale Sparse Linear Equations
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Coefficient matrix of linear equations from finite element method (FEM) is sparse and symmetrical. For the sake of saving CPU operational time and reducing storing requirement to computer, we introduce fully sparse strategy that stores only nonzero elements of symmetrical part by chain pattern. In order to save computational time to accesses data during LU factorization, we develop a symbol LU factorization method. It can minimize fill-in elements and reduce computational quantity of LU factorization. By an address index system and minimum full-in elements algorithm, efficiency of LU factorization can be improved significantly. Numerical experiments show that combination of the symbol LU factorization method and fully sparse storage structure can improve the algorithmic efficiency for FEM solution of large scaled sparse linear equations.

articleTitle: Study on GPS Scattering at Large Angle from Rough Sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The classical Kirchhoff approximation (KA) is modified by introducing the tapered plane wave which is usually used in the method of moment (MOM) for calculating electromagnetic scattering from rough sea surface into the classical KA to make the results by the KA have a high accuracy. Also the definition of the bistatic scattering coefficient of the modified KA and the MOM are unified. Then the electromagnetic scattering characteristic of the GPS signal from rough sea surface under low sea condition is studied by the modified KA and its empirical model of the scattering coefficient at the large scattering angle by interpolating the results calculated by the modified KA is constructed.

articleTitle: Microstrip-fed monopole antenna for UWB application
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we propose a planar microstrip-fed monopole antenna for UWB applications. The proposed antenna is designed from 3 to 20 GHz with VSWR below 2. By adding elliptical shaped cuts between monopole and the feed line, and add notch in the ground plane, the proposed antenna exhibits excellent broadband properties and stable radiation patterns. The proposed antenna has a size of 30times21 mm, and provides ultra-wide bandwidth from 3.0 to 20 GHz in order to satisfy the requirements of the current wireless communications systems. Meanwhile, by introducing a spurline on the feeding line, a narrow band-rejection operation can be realized.

articleTitle: Selection of electromagnetic models for thin-wire antenna analysis
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The electromagnetic calculation techniques have been developed over the years for the numerical solution of antennapsilas temporal transient response. In this paper, a marching-on-in-time algorithm for solving EFIE is presented. The selection of electromagnetic models and spatial basis function is discussed. The time domain results are obtained and compared to illuminate the selection and applied range of two different models.

articleTitle: A broadband FFT processor core based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of a real-time FFT processor based on FPGA, which uses the radix-4 DIF (decimation-in-frequency) algorithm. Five stages of radix-4 butterflies are used to make up of a pipeline to compute the 1024-point complex FFT. The FFT processor can operate at 164MHz and compute a 1024-point FFT at 6.225μs when operating on the device of Xilinx Virtex II Pro 70. This will accommodate a high data throughput transmitted to the back end instrument.

articleTitle: The MPSK signals modulation classification based on Kernel methods
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a new classification method based on Kernel Fisher Discriminant Analysis(KFDA) is brought forward in the MPSK signals modulation classification. The fourth order cumulants of the received signals are used as the classification vector firstly, then the kernel thought is used to map the feature vector impliedly to the high dimensional feature space and linear fisher discriminant analysis is applied to signal classification. The two classifiers based on kernel function - Support Vector Machine and Kernel Fisher Discriminant Analysis are introduced in detail. In order to build effective and robust SVM and KFDA classifiers and compared with each other, the radial basis kernel function is selected, one against one or one against rest of multi-class classifier is designed, and method of parameter selection using cross-validating grid is adopted. Through the experiments it can be concluded that compared with SVM classifier, KFDA can get almost the same classification accuracy and requires less time.

articleTitle: A new approach to multiply windows frequency estimation using neural network
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Technique of multiple windows frequency estimation integrating SVD offers a efficient method which estimate interference temperature in radio frequency environment. Since this paper uses a way which SVD integrate the neural network, the complexity of tradition arithmetic was predigested and improved the nicety of estimating interference temperature. At the same time, the paper provides a good method for estimating the real time interference temperature in complex radio frequency environment.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic modelling of ship classification in OTHR
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Because of the Faraday rotation effect in the ionosphere, the elliptical polarization high frequency electromagnetic wave is used to simulate the sky wave to illuminate the ship targets. The half space FDTD method is utilized to model the ship targets on ocean which have the similar structures. The backscattered instantaneous polarization information of the targets can help to classify targets. The computer simulation results show this method not only can classify them, but also can distinguish the targets motion direction.

articleTitle: Implementation of FDM in solving EM field problem over exact solution and accuracy analysis
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper is a discussion on the implementation of finite difference method (FDM) in solving electromagnetic (EM) field problem. The iterative method and successive over relaxation (SOR) method is discussed and implemented as a technique of FDM. Here the exact solution, using separation of variables is also discussed and implemented. And finally, a comparison of accuracy is shown and discussed among these methods.

articleTitle: Design of a novel TH-UWB signal generator based on 0.18-μm CMOS process
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel time-hopping ultra wideband (TH-UWB) signal generator is designed for TH-UWB communications. The generator consists of a 4-GHz oscillator and a switch with CMOS transmission gates. Through controlling the low frequency signals with time-hopping pulse position modulation (TH-PPM), the circuit outputs TH-UWB signals with wavelets. Implemented in 0.18-μm CMOS technology, the generator provides the amplitude of 65mV at 50Ω load from a 1.8-V supply, and can directly drive an antenna by a transmission line. Meanwhile, the output impedance is matched to 50Ω. The simulation results indicate that the performance of the generator is good and meets the standard of IEEE 802.15.3a.

articleTitle: Study on electromagnetic properties and microwave absorbing characteristics of carbon nanofibers
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this study, carbon nanofibers (CNFs) with the typical diameter ranging from 100~300 nm were prepared via polymer blended wet-spinning method and subsequent thermal treatment. The complex permittivity (epsiv'-jepsiv"), complex permeability (mu'-jmu") and microwave absorption properties of carbon nanofibers/epoxy composites have been studied in Xband frequency range (8.2-12.4 GHz) using a HP8722 ES network system. epsiv', epsiv", epsiv' and epsiv" are found to increase with increased CNF contents. Measured values of these parameters were used to determine the reflection loss at various sample thicknesses, based on a model of a single-layered plane wave absorber backed by a perfect conductor. The composite with 8 wt% CNFs has shown a maximum reflection loss of -34 dB at 10.5 GHz with the -10 dB bandwidth over the extended frequency range of 8.8-12.4 GHz which covers almost the whole X-band at a thickness of 2.1 mm.

articleTitle: A high linear CMOS GPS front-end design
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A RF CMOS front-end with high linearity for the GPS system is described. The LNA has a single-end input and a differential output, the mixer uses the intermodulation distortion (IMD) sinking technique. The front-end achieved -8.5 dBm input referred IP3 with 29.8 dB power gain, an input 1-dB compression point of -24 dBm, and a noise figure of 1.62 dB, consuming 8 mA from a 1.8 V supply.

articleTitle: The Spectrum Estimation Direction Finding via a Single Port Receiver
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new method of DF (direction finding) using spatial spectrum estimate technology is proposed. Based on the covariance matrix obtained by the weight perturbation algorithm, we propose to use a single port receiver for spatial spectrum estimate DF. In principle, the proposed method is adapted for any eigenstructure algorithm. The computer simulation about spatial smoothing algorithm is made. The simulating result shows that the proposed is efficient and very important to the practical usage.

articleTitle: Interpolation of User-Defined Feed Patterns for Reflector Antennas
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A combination of the two-point linear interpolation and the optimal sampling interpolation (OSI) technique is used to reconstruct the primary pattern of reflector antennas, with the efficiency being demonstrated by an example.

articleTitle: Analysis of metallic wire with variable radius using surface integral equation
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Analysis of metallic wire is a classical topic in computational electromagnetic (CEM). It is very important for wire antennas design and RCS reduction research of metallic wires. Moment method (MOM) based on electric field integral equation (EFIE) is a very effective way to solve metallic wires by meshing them with discrete points. However, traditional MOM mainly focuses on the metallic wires with constant radius. In this paper, higher order MOM is discussed and is used in analysis of metallic wires with variable radius. In order to obtain a higher accuracy than that with MOM based on RWG basis function, higher order polynomial expansion is adopted to approximate the current on the wire. This method can reduce the unknowns of models and make the simulation result more convincing. In order to verify the novel performance of higher-order basis function on the analysis of metallic wire with variable radius, two models are tested with the codes based on this method. In addition, they are also solved by other commercial code to test the accuracy of higher order basis function. Very good consistency of the data curves proves the accuracy and high efficiency of this method.

articleTitle: Estimation of group path in oblique ionospheric propagation
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The ionospheric group path and other parameters are discussed in this paper. Relation between the group path and the receiver location has been illustrated. For oblique propagation, neglecting the geomagnetic field and electron collisions, the estimation model of the virtual height and the initial elevation angle are presented. The virtual height and the initial elevation angle are estimated from the group path. The group path estimated using the analytic model is in agreement with the measured results. It is observed that the ionospheric channel has equity to the transmitter and the receiver from the experiment results. The phenomenon is maybe significant for the HF communications.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo simulation for the prediction of the reliability of the receiver
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A statistical analysis approach, Monte Carlo (MC) method, which is applied to predict the reliability of a receiver, is presented in this paper. The model of amplitude modulated communication system is built in ADS. An approximation for the output signal-to-noise of nonlinear receiver system is given when the input consists of a carrier signal modulated and noise. Probabilistic models based on the measurement data for two kinds of noise are derived from Monte Carlo simulations. Statistical results illustrating the applicability of the present work to predict the performance of a communication system are also presented. At last we discuss the advantages and the further applications of MC method.

articleTitle: Study on Behavior of Female Rat 3 Months after Electromagnetic Pulse Irradiation
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: AIM: The present paper investigated the effect on behavior of female rat 3 months after electromagnetic pulse irradiation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Mature female rats were randomly divided into control group and EMP irradiation group. Rats in the EMP irradiation group were exposed to EMP. The field intensity was 100 KV/m with 1000 pulses. The changes of behavior were observed with step through test and open-field test in rats 3 months after electromagnetic pulse irradiation. Memory retention, Error scores, Accumulative Distance (AD), Accumulative Distance of Leaving the Border (AD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">LB</sub>), Accumulative Distance in the User Defined Area (AD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">UDA</sub>), AD inside the inner circle(AD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">IC</sub>), AT of Resting (AT<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">REST</sub>), AT of Walking (AT<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">WALK</sub>) and AD of Walking(AD<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">WALK</sub>) were recorded. RESULTS: Analysis of step through test indicated that the EMP irradiation group has a significant decrease in memory retention and a significant increase in error scores of the entries into the dark compartment compared with control group (P<0.05). Analysis of open-field test indicated that the activity of the EMP irradiation group has a significant increase compared with control group (P<0.05). CONCLUSION: It is inferred that Electromagnetic pulse irradiation can cause some disorders of behavior of rats, which may induce a significant decrease in the ability of learning memory and a significant increase in the activity in rats 3 months after EMP irradiation.

articleTitle: Mechanism analysis of effect of electrode speed on discharge parameters with fluid mechanics
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Mechanism of electrode approach speed effect on discharge parameters, a hot concern in the field of electrostatic discharge research, is analyzed with basic principles in fluid mechanics. Fast moving speed of electrode generates fluid flow in discharge gap and outside of it, making variation of air pressure state between two electrodes. Reduction of air pressure in the gap, based on analysis and derivation, is the dominate factor resulted in the significant action on discharge parameters by electrode fast moving speed.

articleTitle: Application of a new isotropic absorbing boundary condition (ABC) with PML in optimal chiral absorbing condition research
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new absorbing boundary condition (ABC) with PML for isotropic medium is deduced by functional way without D'Alembertian annihilation or factorization technique. Then, the new ABC is applied to optimal chiral medium absorbing condition research and hollow chiral sphere shielding effectiveness research.

articleTitle: Principle and experiment of air target detection based on Signal Power Disturbance
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper introduces an allocation method for air target detection based on GPS satellites and analyses its fundamental principle. Upon the plenitude study of the characteristic of target information acquisition and information processing of bistatic radar, this paper puts forward a kind of target information acquisition technique called SPD (Signal Power Disturbance) which is different from the typical bistatic radar system. A series of experiments have been done to verify the SPD method.

articleTitle: Receiver scheme for space-time coded CDMA system with multiple antennae
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: By introducing a full-rate space-time block coding (STBC) scheme, a multiuser CDMA system with full-rate STBC is presented. Meanwhile, a low-complexity multiuser receiver scheme is developed, the scheme can make full use of the complex orthogonality of STBC to simplify the high decoding complexity of the existing scheme, it has linear decoding complexity. Compared with those full-diversity space-time block coded CDMA (STBC-CDMA) systems, the presented full-rate STBC-CDMA system can realize full rate transmission, low complexity and form efficient spatial interleaving. Thus the concatenation of channel coding can effectively improve the system performance. Simulation results show that the developed scheme can achieve almost the same performance as the existing scheme. Moreover, on the condition of same system throughput and concatenation of channel code, the proposed full-rate system has lower BER than corresponding full-diversity systems

articleTitle: Numerical research of the radiation of the UWB antenna array
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Applying the electromagnetic numerical method, the radiation characteristic in time domain of the electric-magnetic vibrator combined ultrawideband (UWB) antenna array was investigated. The power pattern and radiated character on main axis of different arrays structure and space were analyzed. The coupling between the antenna units was estimated through comparing it with no-coupling model. The results indicate that the electric-magnetic vibrator combined UWB antenna array can improve antenna direction and radiated character on main axis.

articleTitle: Effect of the revolving table on LPDA radiation characteristics
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The metallic revolving table, which is used to support the antenna during the measurement, greatly affects the radiation pattern of the antenna. In this paper, Log Periodic Dipole Array (LPDA) was simulated with and without the metallic revolving table using commercial software - FEKO. Simulated results in two situations were compared to analyze the effects due to the metallic revolving table. Finally, a method for reducing its effect was presented.

articleTitle: Reliability evaluation of ESM deinterleaver based on sorted DOA difference
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In order to evaluate the reliability of deinterleaving results in electronic support measure (ESM), this paper presents a separability test method referred to as sorted direction of arrival difference test (SDOADT) and introduces the concept of confidence level of direction of arrival (CLDOA). Theoretical analyses and experimental results show that, SDOADT has the ability to examine the separability of each pulse cluster obtained from ESM deinterleaver, and its resolution of test increases rapidly with the augment of the pulse numbers. In addition, the index of CLDOA gives a good assessment to confidence degree of the considered pulse cluster in the DOA dimension. So the information about deinterleaving reliability can be achieved via the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Modeling signal strength variation on earth-space paths using the Venezuelan satellite
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper gives the introduction of one experimental scheme to be implemented in Venezuela using its first own telecommunication satellite to get the characteristic of the radio-link channel in one TTC Station.

articleTitle: The harmonic suppression of LNA
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we designed an amplifier based on the transistor ATF 34143 from Agilent. Networks of input and output with appropriate I/O matching were designed through the ADS design software in order to match the impedance of input and output to 50 Ohm. In addition, special optimizations on noise figure and transmission gain were conducted. To suppress the harmonic, various circuits including LC band-pass filter, LC band-reject filter, parallel coupled microstrip transmission line band-pass filter, DGS (defected ground structure) and negative feedback were designed and verified through ADS simulating. As a result, we concluded a relatively effective method for harmonic suppression.

articleTitle: Comparisons of current distributions in shoe-wearing and barefoot human models with and without clothes
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Currents induced in human feet near a cellular phone base station were calculated by the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method and measured by a parallel plate meter at 1869 MHz. From simulation results and measurement data, it is found that the theory of FDTD method makes a good agreement with the experiment. Layer currents distributed in the human body are also obtained by the FDTD method. It is found that the highest layer currents distributed in the human body occur in the area of the chest. From the layer current profiles, it is also found that the maximum induced body current density is below the excitation threshold level of 1 mA/ cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The impact of clothes on the induced currents is also presented. It is found that there is only a little difference in the magnitude of current distributions between the human model with and without clothes.

articleTitle: Coupling of external electromagnetic field to Printed Circuit Board
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The analysis and study of external electromagnetic field coupling to PCB (Printed Circuit Board) is summarized in the present thesis, which is, in particular, how different conditions in terms of incidence direction, polarizing angle of external magnetic field, length and terminal load capacity of microstrip lines on PCB as well as size of metal plane on PCB have effects on external electromagnetic field coupling to PCB.

articleTitle: Cryptanalysis for embedded systems based on electromagnetism emission
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Aimed at the DES cryptographic system realized by the P89C668 microcomputer, a experiment is processed by applying a differential electromagnetic analysis method, thereby obtaining 48-bit sub-key of the 16th round of DES. In this essay, the relationship between data in CMOS gate circuits and electromagnetism emission is analyzed, with an EM information leakage model of a register established, and the attack effects of the Hamming weight model and Hamming distance model compared. Based on the test result, EM information leakage exists in CMOS integrated circuit during work, and different instructions have different leakage signatures under two leakage models, thus providing a basis for implementing relevant protective measures for the cryptographic systems.

articleTitle: GPU acceleration of the iterative physical optics (IPO) method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we employ the Programmable Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) to accelerate the IPO computation for analyzing the scattering of open cavities. Since the iterative strategy accounts for multiple reflections on the inner wall, the IPO method provides a more accurate solution than the other high frequency asymptotic methods. However, it suffers from a large requirement of simulation time. To date, the GPU featuring inherent parallelism and powerful floating-point capability has become an attractive alternative to the central processing unit (CPU) for some of computation tasks. Therefore, we map the time-consuming parts of IPO into the graphics hardware following the stream programming model, and the CPU carries out the computation of the far field scattering. In addition, the numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Bandstop filter with improved Q factor using novel open-loop patch loaded slotline
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel patch-shaped patch loaded slotline (PLS) to provide a band-rejection property with an improved Q factor is proposed in this paper. It has size of only 28% of conventional dumbbell PLS unit section and 72% of the conventional open-loop PLS unit section, while the Q factor is more than 10.5 times than dumbbell PLS and 3.3 times than the conventional open-loop PLS at the same resonant frequency of 33 GHz. High Q bandstop filters based on the newly proposed PLS with two and three sections are designed and simulated. Both filters have sharp cutoff frequency and high attenuation in the stopband.

articleTitle: Design and measurement of dichroic plate for Quasi-Optical Network
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: With the current and future requirements of microwave and millimetric wave instrumentation, particularly the quasi-optical systems, there has been considerable research effort into low loss dichroics worldwide. This paper presents the design and experimental testing of a dichroic operating in a two-channel multi-reflector quasi-optical network (QON). The dichroic plate is designed to work as a frequency filter in the QON, which transmits at 54 GHz and reflects at 89 GHz. A low insertion loss is achieved both in simulation and in measurement.

articleTitle: Research on the distance equation of the submillimeter radiometer via Lambert W function
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper put forward the distance equation for the SMMW radiometer based on the one for the MMW radiometer. In general case, the transmission attenuation was ignored as the detection distance of the radiometer was studied, because of the faint attenuation in some frequency band. But in the SMMW band, the effects of atmospheric attenuation were very significant. So the attenuation coefficient had been introduced into the distance equation. Then the solution of the equation was proposed by using the Lambert W, which is a transcendental function. Finally the simulation and analysis of the solution were given respectively.

articleTitle: Consideration on radiation from an unbalanced-mode spiral antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper describes the radiation from an unbalanced-mode two-arm spiral antenna, where the antenna arms are defined by the Archimedean spiral function. The input impedance, current distribution, radiation pattern, axial ratio, and gain are investigated. The investigation reveals that the unbalanced-mode spiral radiates a circularly polarized wave over a wide frequency range as the balanced-mode spiral.

articleTitle: FDTD method for EM propagation in plasma with perpendicular magnetic declination
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method employing the Exponential Time Differencing (ETD) scheme is applied to the numerical analysis of anisotropic magnetized plasma with the propagation direction of the electromagnetic wave is perpendicular to the biasing field direction. The ETD-FDTD formulations are derived in detail and are confirmed by computing the reflection and transmission coefficients for the ordinary polarized wave and extraordinary polarized wave through a magnetized plasma layer. Excellent agreement between the numerical results and the exact analytical solutions is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Effects of EMP on Bone Formation of MC3T3-E1 Cells
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of electromagnetic pulse (EMP) on bone formation of MC3T3-E1 cells. Proliferation, ALP activity and mineralized nodule formation were examined in MC3T3-E1 cells after EMP exposure (field intensities: 0 kV/m, 50 kV/m, 400 kV/m, 400 pulses once a day for 7 days). After 50 kV/m EMP exposure, all the parameters of MC3T3-E1 cells were not changed significantly. However, the proliferation, ALP activity and mineralized nodule formation of MC3T3-E1 cells in 400 kV/m EMP exposure groups were decreased. In conclusion, the EMP we used was a possibly harmful factor for bone formation. It may suppress bone formation of MC3T3-E1 cells with higher electric field intensity.

articleTitle: Analysis of the airborne transmission lines and antennas coupling interference
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we present a theory for the problem of electromagnetic field coupling to a transmission line. Through the numerical calculation, some important coupling characters of external field and transmission lines are elicited. As airborne antennas are strong radiation sources, this paper figures out some methods to control electromagnetic interference of transmission lines according to antennaspsila installation place and their characters. The research results of the project will have practical applications to the transmission line interference in the airplane.

articleTitle: Ultra Wideband Filter Design Based on Right/Left-Handed Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel design method of ultra wide filter based on the composite right/left-handed transmission line (CRLH-TL) theory is presented in paper. The composite right/left-handed TL with the high-pass characters of left-handed transmission line (LH-TL) and the low-pass characters of right-handed transmission line (RH-TL) are used to construct the ultra wideband (UWB) bandpass filter. Defected ground structure (DGS) and microstrip interdigital capacitors are introduced to satisfy the necessity of the UWB filter. The many cells composite right/left-handed UWB filters are fabricated and measured. Agreement between simulated and measured responses of these filters is demonstrated.

Index Terms: Increase In The Number Of Cells

articleTitle: Design and implementation for electromagnetic environment automatic testing system
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: an electromagnetic environment testing system is introduced in this paper. From the point of design philosophy, hardware design is presented and overall design of the software is detailed, as well as its characteristics, respectively. Compared with traditional instruments, the proposed testing system has prominent superiorities in data-processing, manoeuvrability, scalability and cost-effectives.

articleTitle: Band tunable microstrip bandpass filter using defected single patch resonator
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Triangular patch resonator bandpass filters with tunable operation are developed to perform nicer filter properties of low passband insertion loss, transmission zeros and wide stopband. With tunable fractal-shaped defection acts as perturbation, filter operation frequency and operation band can be controlled, and the responses of undesired resonant modes are greatly weakened even suppressed. The new design brings filter more function which does not require changing the dielectric substrate or patch size. The designed filters have outstanding advantages of single patch with compact size and without resonator coupling gaps, simple circuit topology, nicer performances, miniaturization and can be easily tuned for more applications. All these features are well popular for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Composite-structure frequency selective surface with tripole elements
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Two composite symmetry structure is proposed in this paper. Based on the integral equation method, the frequency response with large incident angle effect is analyzed. As a result of the numerical analysis, it is shown that the composite symmetry structure with single FSS screen is efficient to stabilize the drift of FSS resonant frequency with the steering of incident angle though transmission loss increased. Especially the structure that the FSS is embedded centrally in the dielectrics has better frequency characteristic with flat top and sharp skirts. The studies have indicated the versatility of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Analyzing multilayer FSS with the mutual admittance and spectral approaches
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) is popularly applied as an electromagnetic filter. Frequency response of a perfect FSS should remain unchanged even if the angle of incidence and polarization vary dramatically. Sometimes, the transmission curve of specific FSS is designed to decrease quickly when it is not in band-pass range. It is difficult for single FSS to achieve the goal. Fortunately, multilayer FSS can be used in this situation. In the paper, the mutual admittance and spectral approaches are used to analyze multilayer FSS.
