Compared with other methods, these approaches have the characteristics of quick convergence and little computational time.

articleTitle: A RC network model for electromagnetic moisture sensing of materials
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A resistor-capacitor (RC) network model of moist substance are presented. FL-based algorithm is applied to compute the dielectric properties of the model, which is very general, and could be applied to two-phase (conductor-insulator) materials. Simulating results show that the dielectric relaxation process of moist substances is non-Debye, and relaxation times of the RC network are obtained by curve fitting of the normalized dielectric constant using a superposition of five Debye relaxation processes. By investigating the microstructure of model, we show that the sensing for microstructure change of the RC network model is in agreement with the literature results of electromagnetic moisture measurement.

articleTitle: New semi-elliptical and trapeziform dipole antennas for ultra-wideband communications
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A microtrip-fed semi-elliptical and trapeziform dipole antenna (MFSETDA) which has a small size of (34 mm × 30.2mm) is presented and designed for ultra-wideband (UWB) communications in this paper. The MFSETDA has large bandwidth covering the frequency from 3.1 to 10.6GHz, radiation patterns similar to those of conventional dipole antennas. The proposed microtrip-fed antenna is easy to be integrated with radio-frequency (RF) /microwave circuitry for low manufacturing cost. The designed band-notched MFSETDA operates from 3.116 to 10.637GHz for voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) ⩽2. By etching a folded U-slot in the funnel-shaped radiating patch, a stopband about 718MHz (from 5.110 to 5.828GHz) using in IEEE 802.11a wireless local area network (WLAN) can be obtained. Simulated results show that these antennas are suitable for UWB applications due to their high performances.

articleTitle: Analysis of H-T junction in rectangular waveguide using the MPSTD algorithm
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the MPSTD algorithm is applied to model the H-T junction in rectangular waveguide. The S parameters of the H-T junction are analyzed by MPSTD. The numerical results indicate that the MPSTD algorithm is accurate and efficient to analyze the H-T junction.

articleTitle: Analysis of the directional characteristic of the parallel coupled printed dipole
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The directional characteristic of the parallel coupled printed dipole is analyzed in this paper. The balun structure is used as the feed structure. The far-field pattern of this antenna is formulated, and an example is simulated by using HFSS. The center frequency of this example operates at 5.5 GHz and it has about bandwidth of 20%. The simulated results demonstrate its directional characteristic.

articleTitle: Design of a novel UHF shorted planar monopole antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel shorted planar monopole broadband antenna. In the light of the planar structure easily conformal to the substrate, the shorting structure and the technique of load-adding, this kind of antenna realizes the miniaturization and has a better bandwidth and radiation compared with the conventional planar monopole antenna. The theoretical parametric analysis of the main structure and simulation results with HFSS show that the antenna meets the conditions of VSWR less than 3, vertical polarization, horizontal omni-directional radiation, radiation gain no less than −20dB and radiation smoothness below 3dB, on the work frequency band ranging from 20MHz to 88MHz. The antenna has a wide application in the UHF communication system. The calculational results derived accord well with the experimental results.

articleTitle: TF/SF formulation for ADI-BOR-FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The total-field/scattered-field (TF/SF) formulation for ADI-BOR-FDTD method is presented. The equation modification for field components neighbouring the TF/SF boundary are given in details. To validate the implementation of the method, the backscatter RCS from a PEC sphere is calculated. Compared with theoretical result, they show good agreement.

articleTitle: Research progress on seismic radio sounding technology
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Electromagnetic monitoring methods are in good graces of the experts on short-term and immediate earthquake prediction. Radio sounding technology is one of the methods which has been studied for more than 10 years in Russia and Japan. The research has showed the functions in revealing the seism-ionospheric coupling mechanism and earthquake prediction. Various ways of radio sounding technology to monitor the seism-ionospheric perturbations at home and abroad are summarized in the paper. The typical experiments methods in radio sounding technology are summarized in this paper. The research progress on mechanism of seism-ionospheric disturbances is concluded. The analysis methods of earthquake precursor information and the results in the study at two different frequencies are introduced contrastively. According to the deficiency of the research on radio sounding technology in China, the suggestions on future development are given.

articleTitle: Research on anti-interference of electromagnetic radiation of elevator’s door control system in anechoic chamber
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: the elevator experimental platform and simulated EMI signal system were built to test anti-interference of radiation in anechoic chamber. The destination was to find the frequency ranges and electric field intension which made the elevator lose its functions. The influence of shielding and ground connection would be researched as well. All the malfunctions would be summarized during the whole experiment. And the reasons of those malfunctions should be found. Some measures were taken to avoid the malfunctions under the electromagnetic interference signals. All the whole experiment provides new ways to keep the safe motion of the elevator equipment in public occasions

articleTitle: 220GHz High Power Terahertz Wave Generation Based on Miniaturized Vacuum Cerenkov Device
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: New micromachining techniques now provide the technology to fabricate vacuum electron devices with dimensions suitable for operation in terahertz region. In this paper, results of theoretical and numerical simulation studies of a MW-class, large diameter terahertz wave generator based on the Cerenkov principle are presented. The device consists of a miniaturized foilless diode as well as an oversized rectangular slow wave structure (SWS) which could support surface wave and provide a strong beam-wave coupling. With the method of Particle-in-cell simulation, we investigated the operating characteristics of a prototype 0.22 THz oscillator. It is found that the steady-state, single-frequency operation in the overmoded situation could be realized by the property of surface wave, and the unique voltage tunable capability proves that the device performs as a forward wave oscillator.

articleTitle: Experimental study on fan-beam cassegarian antenna fed by a 4-element binomial array
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Present paper describes the development of a fan-beam cassegarian antenna unit being fed by a 4-element binomial array with centre frequency of 2.45GHz with a 4 set of well matched microstrip dipole units.

articleTitle: Compact UWB bandpass filter with improved upper-stopband performance using multiple-mode resonator
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a novel ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter (BPF) with compact size and improved upper-stopband performance has been studied and designed using multiple-mode resonator (MMR). The MMR is formed by attaching three pairs of ring open stubs in shunt to a high impedance microstrip line. By simply adjusting the radius of the circles of the ring stubs, the resonant modes of the MMR can be roughly allocated within the 3.1-10.6 GHz UWB band while suppressing the spurious harmonics in the upper-stopband. In order to enhance the coupling degree, two interdigital coupled-lines are used in the input and output sides. Thus, a predicted UWB passband is realized. Meanwhile, the insertion loss is higher than 20.0 dB in the upper-stopband from 11.7 to 33.5 GHz. The design is successfully realized in theory and verified by full-wave EM-simulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of location management for different topology of WiMAX networks
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The IEEE802.16e supporting mobility on fixed Wireless-MAN is supposed to be a promising solution for mobile broad-band wireless access (BWA). By integrating HMIPv6 with IEEE802.16e the performance of the system can be enhanced greatly. The meshed topology in IEEE802.16 standard provides wide market coverage as well as low investments of the facility. In this paper, the cost and delay of traditional location management schemes in wireless Mesh networks are analyzed theoretically and compared with that of the typical cellular networks. The result shows that a more effective location management scheme which is suitable for WiMAX Mesh topology should be proposed so that it can better support the mobility and application of different services.

articleTitle: Study on Ultrastructural Changes of Anterior Pituitary in Rats Exposed to PEMW
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The document is to observe the changes of ultrastructure of endocrine cell in anterior pituitary after being exposed to PEMW to explore the possible injury characteristics. 28 male Sparague-Dawley rats were divided into 4 groups (7 rats in each group), the control group was put in the boxes without irradiation. At 24 h after exposure to PEMW (E=100 kVmiddotm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, 10000, 100000, 300000 pulses), the transmission electron microscope was used to observe the ultrastructural changes of anterior pituitary. The result showed that ultrastructures of anterior pituitary were obviously changed in irradiated groups at 10000 pulses, especially in prolactin cells and growth hormone cells, including evacuation of secretory granule, the mitochondrial vacuolization and distinct dilatation of endoplasmic reticulum. The injury gradually aggravate followed by pulses increase. The changes at 300000 pulses were the most severe. In conclusion, PEMW can lead injury to endocrine cells of anterior pituitary in rats, mitochondria and rough endoplasmic reticulum are the main injured organelles.

articleTitle: The perfectly matched layer boundary condition for unconditionally stable WE-FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A perfectly matched layer (PML) is constructed for two dimensional (2D) unconditionally stable (US) FDTD method based on wave equation. This novel PML preserves unconditional stability of the 2D US-FDTD method and has very good absorbing performance. Numerical results are included to illustrate effectiveness and performance of this new PML.

articleTitle: Combined source simulation method - fictitious medium method for solving anisotropic EEG problems
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An electroencephalography (EEG) problem in bio-electromagnetics is to estimate dipolar current sources inside the brain from the measured electric potential distribution on the scalp surface. Traditional linear algorithms are the low-resolution electromagnetic tomography algorithms (LORETA) including improved ones. It is easy to solve isotropic EEG problems by means of them. But the skull conductivity is anisotropic obviously. In this paper, proposed is a source simulation method combined with the fictitious medium method for solving the anisotropic skull layer problem to obtain the electric potential and field intensity on the cortex. Then it can be connected with LORETA. A good agreement between the numerical result and analytical result of the 4-layer spherical head model has been observed. It is shown that this method is effective and feasible. Its prominent advantages are simple and timesaving. And this numerical computation method is suitable for not only spherical head models but also realistic head models with the thin anisotropic layer.

articleTitle: Solving guided wave modes in plasmonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this study, we present an interfacial operator approach for solving guided wave modes of plasmonic crystals. They are formulated as an eigenvalue problem of the wavenumber along the axis of the crystal. In this formulation, the permittivity and permeability of the metallic component can be arbitrary functions of frequency. Moreover, a coupling interface method is introduced to facilitate accurate treatment of the interface conditions with an arbitrary shape between the metal and host materials. Numerical results are illustrated for different shapes of plasmonic crystals, and physical significance is discussed.

articleTitle: A method to confirm the power of complex electromagnetic environment simulator
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: With the development of the complexity of the electromagnetic environment in the battlefield, the careful check in the complex electromagnetic environment, which is simulated to the actual battle, is strongly needed for the weapon system. This paper shows the authorpsilas own perspective on the problem of complex electromagnetic environment modeling and how to definite radiation power of simulator.

articleTitle: Survey of radar target identification for noise polluted radar measurements
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Itpsilas important to develop reliable approach of radar target identification for low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) situation, especially when the radar is used in battle field. A feature selection method is proposed in this paper. The one nearest-neighbor (1-NN) classifier is used as classifier. The effectiveness of radar target identification based on the methods is investigated in computer simulation for both data sets including standard sample and new data sets, all them are mixed with heavy noise.

articleTitle: The radiation of wire-surface junction objects
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, far-field radiation pattern of wire-surface junction structures such as a monopole on a conducting plane, an open-ended waveguide and horn antenna are computed using the method of moment (MoM). The feed of the horn is a wire connected to the up and bottom surfaces of the waveguide, and the distance of the feed wire to the end of waveguide is λ/4, the wire is excited by an unit voltage source in the middle of it. A new line basis function has been used in MoM. Numerical results are presented using the proposed method, which have excellent agreements to those from the commercial software.

articleTitle: Design of downlink and uplink timeslots switch of the TD-SCDMA wireless repeater
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: For radio access systems based on time division duplex (TDD) mode, like the time division synchronous code multiple access (TD-SCDMA) radio system, frame synchronization is a fundamental feature to minimize interference and therefore optimize the offered traffic capacity. In particular, sub-frame synchronization ensures that uplink and downlink transmission directions are positioned. In this paper a method was proposed to realize accurate control of downlink and uplink timeslots of the TD-SCDMA repeater, thus preventing interference between adjacent downlink and uplink timeslots, where the procedure is performed by sub-frame synchronization and time-delay estimation. The method presented in these pages allows to have a higher reliability and accuracy with respect to the methods described in the UTRAN standard for TDD-LCR.

IEEE Keywords: Time division synchronous code division multiple access

articleTitle: Analysis on the effect of plasma on the transmission characteristics microwave transmit-receive switches
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper the characteristic of plasma in the discharging microwave transmit-receive (TR) switches is analyzed. The transmission characteristics of microwave TR switches are studied when the radar transmits signals and receives signals. The S-parameters of the TR switches are shown in both cases. Finally, the reflection effect of the plasma with different frequency on the incident wave in the resonance slot of the TR switches is discussed .

articleTitle: Impedance analysis of the fragment-type tag antenna using FDTD
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The impedance matching between the tag antenna and the IC chip is a crucial problem attracting increasing attentions recently. This paper firstly presents a study on impedance calculation of a metal strip dipole using finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method with unsplit perfectly matched layer (UPML) absorbing boundary condition. On this basis, the impedance characteristic of the fragment-type tag antenna is analyzed. More accurate results are obtained. Comparisons with the commercial software results show the accuracy and validity of the method.

articleTitle: Development of a coax-to-microstrip transition over the range of 1–15GHz
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a coax-to-microstrip transition incorporating a miniature coaxial connector with glass bead is developed. The transition is firstly simulated with the aid of HFSS and then measured in the frequency range of 1-15 GHz. The simulated and measured results are found in good agreement.

articleTitle: An accurate adaptive method for drawing 2-D electric lines of force
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive method for drawing 2-D electric lines of force of electrostatic field. The proposed method is based on high order Taylor expansion technique. By adaptively controlling the drawing step length, the proposed method can meet high drawing precision requirement. The principle, implementation and prerequisites of the proposed method are discussed. Numerical examples are given to validate the proposed method’s accuracy.

articleTitle: Secure communication of cluster-based ad hoc networks using ID-based cryptography
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Ad hoc networks are more vulnerable to security threats than the traditional wireless networks. A secure communication scheme is proposed based on ID-based cryptography (IBC). The main problems discussed are nodes joining and session key agreement. In a hostile environment, the demand of concealing nodepsilas identity is studied. The proposed scheme uses symmetric cryptography and the properties of bilinear pairing. The analysis shows that the scheme has authentication, confidentiality, non-impersonation, forward security and anonymity properties with less computation and lower communication cost.

articleTitle: MPSTD analysis of metal resonators
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the MPSTD algorithm is applied to model the metal resonators, such as rectangular resonators and coaxial resonators. The resonant frequencies of the metal resonators are analyzed by MPSTD. The numerical results indicate that the MPSTD algorithm is accurate and efficient to analyze the metal resonators.

articleTitle: Improved microstrip coupled-line bandpass filters for spurious responses suppression
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, microstrip coupled-line bandpass filters using a improved SIR configuration are proposed. Conventional microstrip coupled-line filters are very popular for RF front ends because they can be fabricated easily. However, their large harmonic causes the shape of the passband to be asymmetric in the upper band and it worsens the skirt properties. By proper design, the harmonic of improved filters can be significantly suppressed through the use of improved SIR configurations. There are more than 20dB suppression at 2f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and 3 f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. This type of filter can be used to suppress the harmonic without any additional devices and regardless of the substrate.

articleTitle: False response analysis of channelized reconnaissance receiver
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Channelized reconnaissance receiver (CRR) is very important for radar ECCM. The false response caused by the nonlinearity of microwave circuits reduces the dynamic range of the CRR. In this paper, we analyzed the frequency and amplitude characteristic of false response, developed a method to identify the false response with multi-signal input, and chose the optimization intermediate frequency to minimize the false response with single-signal input. Finally, we designed a CRR based on these analyses, which has a large dynamic range more than 90 dB.

articleTitle: Study on a method for steam wetness measurement based on microwave resonant cavity
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A method for wetness measurement based on microwave resonant cavity is presented in this paper. A specially structured resonant cavity with annular grid at its both ends was designed for the wetness measurement of flowing wet air. The pneumatic characteristic of the cavity was simulated and the S parameter of it was measured. The simulation and measurement results show that it is especially suitable for the online measurement of flowing wet air wetness. The measurement system has been developed and used to measure the saturated wet air which is especially produced for studying the performance of the system. The experimental data and theoretical value are compared and the reasons for deviation between them are analyzed. The resolution of the wet air wetness measurement can reach 1.5% in the temperature range of 29~38degC.

articleTitle: A compact fourth order locally one-dimensional FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A numerical dispersion improved locally one-dimensional finite-difference time-domain (LOD-FDTD) based on compact implicit fourth order scheme is proposed in this paper. The numerical dispersion error is shown to be reduced due to the fourth order spatial accuracy. Meanwhile the proposed LOD-FDTD scheme is simpler than its ADI-FDTD counterpart.

articleTitle: A novel TR-STBC-OFDM scheme for Mobile WiMAX system
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a new scheme (namely TR-STBC -OFDM) which combines time-reversal space-time block codes (TR-STBC) with OFDM to derive a new MIMO-OFDM scheme for Mobile WiMAX. As an optimum last-mile access technology, Mobile WiMAX has many unique advantages which make it have the potential to impact the other forms of telecommunications. However, it still faces gigantic challenges, such as lower complexity and efficient system implementation. In addition to the destructive multipath nature of the wireless channels, frequency selective channels pose intersymbol interference (ISI) while offering frequency diversity for successfully designed systems. Since OFDM scheme can combat ISI extremely well and the TR-STBC scheme has full-diversity and full-rate as well as its lower computation complexity, the scheme in this paper performs effectively. Simulation results show that compared with the orthogonal space-time block codes combined with OFDM (O-STBC-OFDM) scheme which is recommended by IEEE802.16e specifications, this novel scheme can achieve better tradeoff between elegant BER performance, simple decoding as well as lower computation complexity for Mobile WiMAX system.

articleTitle: Dual band microstrip antenna with triangular tuning stub for WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents the microstrip antenna with triangular tuning stub which designed and simulated by using IE3D program. This antenna is designed for 50 Ohms impedance microstrip line for dual band frequency, 2.297–2.952 GHz and 5.138–6.051 GHz which supports WLAN communications coverage IEEE 802.11b/g (2.4–2.4835 GHz), IEEE 802.16a (5.15–5.35 GHz) and IEEE 802.16d (5.7–5.9 GHz). The bandwidth at lower resonance frequency of this antenna is 0.655 GHz, while upper resonance frequency is 0.913 GHz. The simulation results show that the lower and upper resonance frequencies are agreed with the measurement results.

articleTitle: A New Algorithm about Transforming from Near-field to Far-field of Radar Target Scattering
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In order to meet the approximate plane-wave irradiating condition, adequate large field or compact range system is needed for RCS measurement of large aircraft targets. However, an outside testing field site or a compact range system is very expensive, so a new RCS extrapolation method named Hankel algorithm based on near-distance testing has been presented. According to the fact that objective reflectivity spatial distribution is unchanged with measurement state in ISAR imaging, here the multi-scattering center model is built. Then, the height of stealth target is always short, and the far-field condition can easily be satisfied on vertical plane, so the incident spherical wave is equivalent to cylindrical wave. Once more, the relationship between far-field and near-field is deduced by regarding image of the target as secondary radiating source. Finally, the RCS of target can be obtained with the scattering information of near-field extrapolated at full angular aspect. Taking derivative of the near-field data with respect to frequency in algorithm, the error can be reduced in simplifying formula, and just meet the requirement of stepped-frequency system. The results of simulation and experiments show that the algorithm is precise as well as effective.

articleTitle: TGR analysis of a kind of grounding electrode
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper discussed the transient Grounding Resistance(TGR) of a kind of simple earthing electrode. In order to study the influence of TGR, a kind of TGR testing system is adopted, which is testing the TGR under impulse current. In this paper, the round steel are utilized as the material of the earthing electrode. In addition, the TGR is calculated using FDTD method. The waveform and results of calculated with FDTD is similar to the measured results. Therefore, the accurry of the experimental system is proved. The experimental results have practical value in the project.

articleTitle: A Novel UWB Planar Antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a novel ultra wideband (UWB) planer antenna is proposed. The antenna is composed of a square ring radiator and partially grounded, which occupies about 3.5 GHz impedance bandwidth covering 5.9 GHz-9.4 GHz. A quasi-omnidirectional and quasi-symmetrical radiation pattern in y-z plane in the whole frequency band is also obtained. The antenna satisfies the requirements of UWB wireless communications verified with the results presented, and will be a good solution for some UWB applications.

articleTitle: Low cost, low side-lobe array of waveguide-fed microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A low-cost, low side-lobe Ku-band array of microstrip antennas, which is fed by waveguide, is presented in this paper. The 72 corner-fed square patches of the array are arranged in a 6-by-12 configuration. A novel waveguide to microstrip line transition with power divider is employed as a centre fed for the array in order to reduce the loss of the microstrip feed line. The gain of the array was measured to be 24.1 dB. The side-lobe is below -20 dB and the return loss at resonant frequency is less than -25 dB. This array of waveguide-fed microstrip antennas can be used in many modern communication systems, such as a mobile radar sensor, in which the transition can be fixed as a connection between the module with a front-end waveguide and antennas.

articleTitle: Theoretical analysis and simulation of the outage probability for six-state Markov model on land-mobile satellite channels
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An analytical technique well suited to numerical analysis is presented for computing the average outage probability of binary phase-shift keying (BPSK) and binary differential phase-shift keying (DPSK) in the land-mobile satellite channel (LMSC). The close-loop formulas are found for not using diversity and L-branch micro-diversity using maximal ratio combining (MRC). Following previous empirical studies, the LMSC is modelled as a six-state Markov model. Using measurement channel parameters, the performance in mobile environment for six-state Markov model is found.

articleTitle: Modelling the Radio Wave Propagation in the Troposphere with Discrete Mixed Fourier method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Application of the discrete mixed Fourier transform method to solve the narrow angle parabolic equation with impedance boundary condition is presented, and this method is used to investigate the properties of radio propagation in atmospheric duct. In the process of discretization of auxiliary function, traditional central difference formula is replaced by backward difference formula, this make the numerical results more stable. The research lays the theoretical foundation for studying the radar detection performance, radar detection shadow zone and forecast of atmospheric duct.

articleTitle: Analysis of crosstalk in PCB design
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Crosstalk is an important EMC problem in printed circuit board design. A wildly used theoretical model based on transmission line theory is presented in this paper. On this basis, the origin and some characters of crosstalk and the factors affecting crosstalk are introduced. The simulation software HyperLynx is applied to analyze the factors. From simulated results, some design features that will reduce crosstalk are concluded.

articleTitle: Analysis of dual-frequency monopole antenna using FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel dual-frequency monopole patch antenna for WLAN applications is presented and demonstrated in this paper. Its operating mode centered at about 2.4GHz and 5.2GHz. The antenna is analyzed by the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method. The simulated and measured results are presented. The measured 10dB bandwidths achieved were 780MHz (2.16GHz∼2.94GHz) and 1.05GHz (4.74GHz∼5.80GHz) at 2.4GHz and 5.2GHz, respectively. The antenna also has the properties of simple structure, small dimension, easier to manufacture, and low cost.

articleTitle: A cross layer selective approach for wireless image transmission system over fading channels
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a cross layer selective approach for wireless image transmission system over fading channels. We extract the key information of the image first and transmit the key information over good channel condition to ensure that most of the errors are shifted to the elementary part of the image. Exact relationship between SNR and Peak SNR (PSNR) of the received image is presented. Simulations are conducted with different Signal to Noise Ratios (SNR) and different thresholds. It is shown that the proposed approach can significantly improve the transmission quality. For example, at SNR=5dB with Rayleigh flat fading channel with BPSK, the Peak SNR of the received image transmitted by the proposed approach has a gain of 7dB over the normal approach1.

articleTitle: Synthesis of the Shaped-beam Array Antennas Using Hybrid Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A hybrid genetic algorithm (GA) for optimization of beam forming in linear array antennas is presented in this paper. This algorithm is the combination of GA and direct search method, which emphasizes the global optimization characters of GA and avoids the slightly random fluctuate using GA when the result closes to perfect. Simulations were performed for synthesizing a low side-lobe cosecant squared beam antenna array and a wide beam antenna array. The results show the hybrid GA is effective.

articleTitle: Efficient parallel adaptive beamforming algorithm for planar array system
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: For large planar adaptive arrays, the computational load and the terabyte data transmission are two challenging problems in the implementation of adaptive beamforming system. This paper considers the problem of designing an efficient parallel adaptive algorithm using the two dimensional(2D) planar array. This paper extends the efficient parallel adaptive beamforming algorithm based on LCMV to adaptive 2D sensor array processing. The proposed 2D parallel adaptive algorithm can be easily implemented in distributed-parallel-processing system due to its parallel structure. It can save the data transmission as well as computing cost.

articleTitle: A novel ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter using MIM CRLH transmission line structure
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: UWB Communication systems demand for ultra-wideband filters of bandwidth of up to 110%, which is challenging to achieve for a compact and low-cost design with conventional materials. This paper presents a novel ultra-wideband (UWB) bandpass filter design using composite right/left-handed transmission line (CRLH TL) structure. In addition, to further simplify the design and reduce the size, metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitors and stub inductors are employed. The simulated results demonstrate the negative permittivity and permeability of the composite materials used and show that the filter with an insertion loss of less than 1.0 dB throughout the pass band of 2.8 to 10.2 GHz. The variation of group delay is around 0.20 ns over the most central band which is small enough for the filter to be used in an impulse radio UWB system.

articleTitle: Doppler radar sensing system of respiration and heart rate
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, Doppler radar system is designed, which is composed of oscillator, mixer, LNA, and antennas. The idea of this paper is using reverse circular polarization for bio-detection Doppler radar to selectively receive signals reflected from highly conductive body surfaces. To improve isolation property between transmitter and receiver, we use the bistatic system using LHCP and RHCP antennas. The budget of system is analyzed and the experimental results are discussed.

articleTitle: Research on wide beamwidth and high gain quasi-Yagi antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The principle of Quasi-Yagi antenna is introduced and the influences of different structure parameters. CST Microwave Studio is used to simulate and optimize the antenna. The influence of antenna parameters is researched and the antenna is manufactured. The simulation and measurement of the antenna show that 2.9-3.8 GHz band with the VSWR less than 2 is obtained, and gain is more than 6 dB in plusmn60deg of H plane, plusmn15deg of E plane. Wide beamwidth and high gain is obtained.

articleTitle: A broadband linear phased array based on mutual coupling
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: a broadband phased array based on intentionally introduce mutual coupling between the periodic elements is designed and presented in this paper. The design conception is fundamentally different from the design of the traditional broadband arrays. Simulated results and partially measured results show that the array can be used to obtain wideband impedance and pattern bandwidth.

articleTitle: A novel stacked wideband microstrip patch antenna with U-shaped parasitic elements
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a novel wideband microstrip patch antenna with U-shaped parasitic elements stacked with two rectangular patches on a separate layer is proposed. The antenna is simulated by the full-wave electromagnetic simulator and the results of the performance of the proposed antenna are investigated. The antenna input impedance bandwidth is 33% (4.7-6.62 GHz) with respect to the centre frequency of 5.68 GHz. The controlled frequency includes the 802.11a (5.15-5.825 GHz) band, and the antenna proposed can be used for wireless LAN. The antenna is designed on a small size ground plane (25 mm times 30 mm ) for application of compact transceivers.

articleTitle: Passive observation mode study in ionospheric vertical sounding
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper details a new passive observation mode in ionospheric vertical sounding based on CADI ionosonde platform. The realization of the new observation mode not only alleviate the congestion problem of the ionospheric high frequency channel, but also provide a economical and effective method for the ionosphere monitoring and studying.

articleTitle: A Solution to the Propagation of Electromagnetic Wave in plasma Sheath Using FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: An auxiliary differential equation finite-difference time domain (ADE-FDTD) methodology was used here to study the propagation of electromagnetic wave through a plasma sheath The reflection and transmission coefficients calculated by ADE-FDTD were compared with the analytic ones. The result shows an excellent agreement. Then, ADE-FDTD was used to resolve wave propagation in plasma sheath of RAMC flight, and the FDTD results agree with the date measured by RAMC flight.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of radar echo signal of aircraft targets with GRECO
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, the complex RCS at several frequency in a certain bandwidth of the given target is simulated by GRECO method, which is based on the physical optics (PO) method and physical theory of diffraction (PTD) method, and the HRRP of the target is calculated with these wideband responses. By convoluting transmission pulse of the given radar and the HRRP of the target, the echo signal of the given target with the given radar can be obtained. The proposed technique is validated, and simulation results for an aircraft model is given.

articleTitle: Phase Unwrapping for Multibaseline SAR Interferometry Using Optimized Data
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, a new method of the multibaseline interferometric SAR phase unwrapping based on the model of the optimum data vector is introduced. The method constructs the multibaseline optimal weighted joint data (MOWJD) vector by taking advantage of the coherence information of neighboring pixels in order to adaptively coregister the SAR images and then employ the projection of the joint signal subspace onto the corresponding noise subspace to estimate the unwrapped interferometric phases (or the terrain heights).Theoretical analysis and experimental results show that the method can provide the accurate unwrapped interferometric phase even if the coregistration error is close to one pixel. The effectiveness and robustness of the technique is verified by simulated data.

articleTitle: The study of the symmetry of multipath parameters
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The study of multipath signal is very important in the area of wireless communications. However, the past study mainly focused on how to reduce the influences of multipath on communication signals. In this paper, considering the law of symmetry in information obtaining, the possibility and method of enabling both sides to obtain parameters from multipath signals is presented. Since the parameters which are symmetrical to both sides not only contain the natural information of the channel, but also contain the certainty of both sides, so they are valuable in many fields.

articleTitle: Analysis of radiated emissions from multiconductor lines
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A case of three-conductor lines is analyzed. The currents in multiconductor transmission lines (MTL) are solved from MTL equation; then, electric dipole sequences and mirror methods are used to estimate the total radiated emissions (RE) induced by these currents. The simulations show that RE of MTL is nonlinear to the one of single circuit. The electric field intensity of MTL is about 1∼3 dB smaller than the sum of RE of single circuit, and the difference become larger as the raising of frequency.

articleTitle: A Novel Implementation of Truncation Number for Improving Accuracy of MLFMA
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: For multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA), we develop a novel method that adopted different precision control in different levels for truncation number calculation and investigate the effect on calculation precision caused by nodes number in detail used in the two-dimensional Lagrange interpolation, we improve the interpolation method which chose different nodes number in different levels. The improvement could enhance the precision and efficiency of calculation notably concluded from the numerical results. It could meet the algorithm requirement of electromagnetic scattering for complex three-dimensional targets.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable multiple-band antenna using switches
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A reconfigurable multiple-band planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) integrated with switches is presented. Two switches are inserted into the T-shaped slot on rectangular patch and by making these two switches ON and OFF the effective electrical length of the antenna could be changed. The antenna can work not only at GSM, but also DCS, PCS, Bluetooth/WLAN 2.4 GHz bands. This reconfigurable antenna with the characteristics of light weight, small dimension and low cost, can be used in multiple-band for integrated wireless communication system.

articleTitle: Co-array properties of minimum redundancy linear arrays with minimum sidelobe level
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Minimum redundancy linear arrays (MRLA) are widely used in radio astronomy, microwave radiometry, radar and other fields. Based on the Fourier properties of arrays with optimal co-array properties, the co-array properties of MRLAs with minimum sidelobe level are presented for the first time, validated by simulations of different MRLAs with 5~9 elements. The upper bound of the peak sidelobe level (PSL) of a MRLA is also derived.

articleTitle: Parallel implementation of the split-field FDTD method for the analysis of periodic structure
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The periodic structure can be analyzed by using the split-field FDTD method. But when the very fine grid is involved, more memory and time are required, sometimes it even canpsilat be calculated on single PC machine. In this paper we present the parallel implementation of the split-field FDTD method based on the message passing interface(MPI), which solves the memory and speed problems, and give out a new method based on the conversation of energy, so as to verify the accuracy and the efficiency. We also compare the results of the serial split-field method with the proposed method.

articleTitle: The designing of a broad stopband HTSC filter using CMRC
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Using the method of full-wave analysis, a HTSC CMRC (compact microstrip resonant cell) is designed with the assistance of CAD. And an eight-pole quasi-elliptic filter is designed using the CMRC. It is manufactured, installed and measured. The measured result is provided.

articleTitle: The microwave interferometer on J-TEXT tokamak
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A 2 mm microwave interferometer is developed to measure plasma electron density for the J-TEXT tokamak. The interferometer views the plasma vertically through a set of large diagnostic ports and the system is configured as a frequency-modulated interferometer. The interferometer routinely provides real-time feedback control for the gas injection system.

articleTitle: Design and implementation for signal integrity trouble diagnosing system
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper proposes a troubling diagnosing system for analyzing signal integrity and describes a complete architecture for the system with the crucial software for scanning and controlling. The software is developed with the software LabVIEW 8.5 from the National Instruments. The paper also describes the implementation of the data processing and displaying the radiation graph. Moreover, the result is resented from scanning a part of an actual main board from an operating computer with the system in the end.

articleTitle: Simple and accurate radio frequency inductance expression for on-chip planar spiral inductors
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A simple and accurate expression for calculating radio frequency (RF) inductance of square, hexagonal, octagonal and circular on-chip planar spiral inductors is presented in this paper. The expression presented shows a functional relationship between RF inductance (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RF</inf>) and some certain electrical parameters of inductors, which are low frequency inductance (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>), self resonant frequency (ƒ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">R</inf>), work frequency (ƒ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">W</inf>) and substrate material correlation coefficient (β). Compared with both three-dimensional field solver simulation data and experiment data, the RF inductance data obtained by the presented expression matched both of them typically within around 5%. So it is worth expecting that this expression would be very useful for designing and optimizing of inductors, especially for applying inductors to RF ICs.

articleTitle: Study of moving phase center antenna arrays using the FDTD method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Time modulated linear antenna arrays consisting of printed dipoles above a ground plane are simulated using the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. The FDTD method brings great convenience to the investigation of the time domain responses of moving phase center antenna arrays. In conjunction with the near-to-far field transformation in time domain, the far-field transient response can be computed to explain the physical essence of time modulated linear arrays with bidirectional phase center motion (BPCM). By employing the discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and the frequency domain near-to-far field transformation, the radiation patterns at the frequencies of interest are obtained and are compared with the measured results. Simulation results show that the FDTD method is an effective and accurate approach for the full-wave simulation of time modulated antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Long-data DFT and its application in radar reconnaissance receiver
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Limited by the computing speed of FFT (Fast Fourier Transform), Short-data DFT(Discrete Fourier Transform) is often used in radar reconnaissance digital receiver. But for larger N, the number of sample points, is selected, not only windows effect is reduced and frequency resolution is improved, but also export that the frequency domain signal to noise ratio is N times increase of time-domain. So when N is a greater value, using DFT measuring frequency algorithm can detect small signal submerged in the noise. A realization scheme is given based on the big point DFT radar reconnaissance digital receiver, and export the quantitative relationship about sense pulse modulation radar signals. With the development of component technology and improvement of algorithm, long-data DFT has sufficient computing speed now, which provides the probability of its application in digital receiver. Long FFT use generally 2-dimension algorithm and its implementation method on FPGA are also talked about.

articleTitle: Influence of atmosphere on detection of remote aerial target using passive ground-based radiometer
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Focused on the detection model of the remote aerial target using ground-based radiometer, the influence of atmosphere has been analyzed in this paper in detail. Firstly the mechanism of atmospheric influence on the detection has been discussed by modelling a detection model of aerial target using passive ground-based radiometer. Secondly, according to the inhomogeneous vertical profile of atmosphere, a layered atmosphere model has been introduced and corresponding formulas of atmospheric attenuation and radiation has also been presented. Thirdly, the model has been validated by the experimental data using 8 mm passive ground-based radiometer. At last, supported by the curves adopting MATLAB simulation, the influence of atmosphere has been analyzed and some suggestions about radiometer design are provided. The conclusion in this paper can be a valuable reference for passive detection of aerial target.

articleTitle: A new PBG suspended patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A new suspended patch antenna with PBG structure is presented, and antenna performances are optimized, simulated and analyzed. Compared with a common patch antenna and a suspended patch antenna, the new PBG one is shown with the radiation pattern convergent and the front radiation enhanced, and the surface wave suppression and antenna performance improvement by PBG are demonstrated. The new PBG antenna possesses a relative bandwidth of 4.92%, which increased 3.89% and 1.46% compared with a common patch antenna and a suspended one, respectively. Simultaneously, obtains a E-plane gain and a H-plane gain of 11.42dB and 10.96dB, respectively, and both increased more than 2dB compared with the common patch antenna and the suspended patch antenna.

articleTitle: Integrative modeling and analyses of the wireless link for communication system in railway environment
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The FDTD method and the ray-tracing method are combined to study the characteristic of the wireless link of railway communication system in 900 MHz band. FDTD method is used for computing field in near region where a more realistic high-speed railway environment including the locomotive, antennas, steel rails, earth plane and the conducting wire for power supply, is modeled in detail. The ray-tracing method is used for transformation field from far region to near region. The variations of the output voltage and current of the monopole antenna mounted on locomotive with the train location on railway are given. The objective of this paper is to study the relationship between the incident wave and the output voltage and current with the influence of the complicated high-speed railway environment considered.

articleTitle: Analysis and simulation of RF MEMS switch
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Along with the fast development of the automotive electronics technology, the wireless communication technique on vehicles has huge market potential. This paper takes the cantilever beam MEMS switch as an example to discuss mechanical principle and function simulation of the RF MEMS switch used in Vehicle-carried radio frequency communication. We select three kinds of cantilever beams with different section to analyze their switch characteristics, compute and use ANSYS software to carry out multi-physical coupling analysis and simulation. The threshold voltage, inherent frequency and optimal design of three kinds of beams are also discussed. The results provide a satisfactory theoretical support to design various high performance RF MEMS switches with variational section beam.

articleTitle: Range sidelobes suppression for HF surface wave radar with discontinuous spectra
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In order to improve the anti-interference performance, the high-frequency surface wave radar uses several discontinuous clear frequency bands for transmission. Spectral discontinuity causes high range sidelobes which influence detecting and identifying the targets. A novel modified CLEAN algorithm is proposed to remove the sidelobes interferences of the equivalent matched processing result of the received signals. The simulation results show that the method can not only suppress the range sidelobes efficiently but also enhance the range resolution greatly.

articleTitle: Analysis of field-to-transmission line coupling in the airplane
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper classifies the field-to-transmission line coupling problems in the airplane into two different subsections according to the relationship between the frequency of incident field and the length of transmission line. In the high frequency case, distributed sources are introduced to derive the current response of two-wire transmission lines excited by random electromagnetic field in terms of transmission line theory. Finally to investigate the validity and accuracy of this method, compute the terminal current of specific parameters on the Matlab simulating circumstance, and compare the results with other methods. This proposed method extends the transmission line theory to a new application area, and provides some reference for equipment-level and system-level electromagnetic compatibility design in the airplane.

articleTitle: Efficient characterization of RF sources for the design of noise suppression filters
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The filter development process, to reduce occurring conducted emissions, is still an unsolved problem within EMC considerations, due to the filter attenuation depends on the impedance values of the device under test. The paper presents a method how to characterize arbitrary active applications within the frequency domain. The evaluated noise sources are described as Y or Z- matrices with additional active sources in respect to Theveninpsilas law. Through a translation from the time into the frequency domain even circuits including non-linear elements can be considered. The method is presented for the example of a power stage circuit and it is considered how to translate the technique into measurements.

articleTitle: A novel method of passive harmonic wave suppression based on frequency selection for waveguide filter
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A novel method of passive counteraction technique is proposed to suppress harmonic waves of waveguide filter. The method is to attach a new one-port device to pass harmonic waves only and then echo them to counteract the waves in the direction of transmission. The general design procedure and its technical details are studied, especially the skills how to set the position of the probes. Experiments prove that the method is easy to adapt the traditional waveguide filter to achieve wide stop band, both 2nd and 3rd spurs are below −20dB overall.

articleTitle: Adaptive transmit power allocation scheme for V-BLAST system under imperfect channel state information
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: We propose an adaptive transmit power allocation (ATPA) scheme for vertical Bell laboratories layered space-time (V-BLAST) system in the presence of channel state information (CSI) imperfection. The proposed ATPA scheme is aimed at minimizing the bit error rate (BER). At the transmitter, subjected to the total transmit power constraint, the proposed ATPA scheme is used to allocate proper power for every sub-stream based on imperfect channel state information (I-CSI) and the statistical characteristic of channel estimation errors. At the receiver the modified minimum mean square error (MMSE) detector which takes into account the errors of channel estimation is used to remove the co-antenna interference (CAI) in order to improve BER performance further. Simulation results show that the proposed ATPA algorithm is effective for V-BLAST system under imperfect CSI, the BER performance is better than that with equal power allocation. Moreover, corresponding capacity is approximate equal to that of equal power allocation scheme.

articleTitle: A new wideband differentially-driven microstrip antenna with H-shape slot and U-shaped ground
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: We introduce a new microstip antenna with the use of H-shape slot .we make use of the higher order mode radiation in addition to the intrinsic domain mode, yielding a very wide impedance bandwidth, which can reach to about 50%. Most importantly, with the use of a U-shaped ground, we can make the gain more stable, which is very important in modern devices.

articleTitle: A 26–40GHz monolithic doubly-balanced mixer
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 26-40 GHz monolithically integrated doubly-balanced mixer for ultra-high speed wireless communication. A modified Marchand balun is used to expand the bandwidth. A coupled line of U section improves the port to port isolation and provides the IF-output port. Simulated in 0.15-mum GaAs PHEMT technology, the mixer achieves a low conversion loss of less than 8 dB and a high isolation of above 30 dB over a 26-40 GHz RF/LO bandwidth and a 8-14 GHz IF bandwidth.

articleTitle: Prediction of signal transfer characteristics of probe card using electro-magnetic solvers
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Probe card is an interface to test the operation of fabricated semiconductor wafer. It connects the test/measurement device to semiconductor wafer by redistributing thousands of signal routes in an appropriate way. In this paper, we measure and simulate the high-frequency transfer characteristics of a MEMs type Probe Card. By comparison of the simulated and measured data, it is confirmed that Electro-Magnetic Solvers (HFSS, SIwave, and Nexxim for integration) are reliable to predict the high frequency signal transfer characteristics of the complicated MEMs probe card. Also, it was found that the major signal attenuation occurred at the tip and PCB in the Probe Card, especially in high-frequency range.

articleTitle: Microwave absorbers based on local resonance of metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper, two kind of microwave absorbers based on local resonance of artificial periodic structures i.e. metamaterials. When irradiated by plane wave with adaptive polarization, there will be electric or magnetic local resonance in the metamaterials. To absorb the microwave energy been reflected, resistive sheets are used like conventional Salisbury screen. The absorber based on electric resonance is very thin and easy to fracture. The two relevant features of the magnetic resonance absorber are its electrical thickness is very small while compared with the operating wavelength, and the absence of a metallic backing, which is a common part of conventional absorber layouts. The full-wave simulations presented in the paper using FEM method confirm the effectiveness of the proposed absorbers for microwave applications.

articleTitle: Prediction of in-flight aircraft radar cross-section
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper describes a model which simulates and predicts the dynamic radar cross section (RCS) for a moving aircraft. The model simulates the radar-aircraft engagement dynamics modelling the aircraft motion and the physical aircraft vibrations which will effect in-flight aircraft radar cross section. High frequency techniques are used for target scattering calculations. Along with the description of the dynamic situations and aircraft scattering calculations, a typical simulation was performed and the output quantities are shown.

articleTitle: Research on practical model for high atmospheric refractive index in a certain region
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Based on measuring datum from weather observation equipments, the variable rules and characteristics of atmospheric refractive index are analyzed. According to that, the accurate model for high atmospheric refractive index within 9km is founded, and the accuracy of this model is examined according to weather explore datum.

articleTitle: The effects of mechanical tolerances on multi-aperture waveguide directional couplers
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Mechanical tolerances of the coupling apertures in a 8 mm multi-aperture waveguide directional coupler (MAWDC) introduced by the manufacturing process lead to a variation in the device performance such as the directivity and the coupling value. To obtain this variation by repeated experiments of large numbers of randomly perturbed geometries is excessively costly. An alternative is to find the changing rule of the performance with respect to each geometric variable. It is cheaply available over the whole frequency band when the appropriate theory of coupling by apertures is used for the analysis. In this study, an accurately designed millimetre wave MAWDC working from 26.5 GHz to 40 GHz is fabricated. By contrast with the original designed coupler, a series of coupling walls with different dimension tolerances and position tolerances from 0.05 mm to 0.2 mm in the apertures are manufactured. Results are presented when these coupling apertures have different tolerances. The changing rules of the performance are also obtained.

articleTitle: The error cause analysis in EM simulation of ship
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: To ensure validity and applicability of computation results, the EM characteristic of a ship must have a full embodiment in the simulation. In this paper, concerning EM environment, configuration feature and RF function requirements of a ship, illustrates EM characteristic and error cause from two aspects, i.e.EM simulation model, computation and analysis method. Aiming at a typical example, analyzes the error in EMC simulation and RCS computation. It is proven that complex EM characteristics of a ship bring huge difficulty to accurate simulation, and the simulation modal and computation method are tightly connected to ensure the veracity of the simulation results.

articleTitle: Passive millimeter wave radiometric measurement of metal solid objects
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: On basis of analyzing the antenna temperature contrast of metal solid objects, the passive millimeter wave radiometric measurement was presented for concealed body technology. In the experiment the metal solid object was under the condition of naked and covered with weft by a 94GHz dicke-type radiometer. The sky temperature was also given by the former measurement. The results show the antenna temperature contrast of the metal solid object has great changes under the two different conditions and the passive millimeter concealed body technology is really to reduce the contrast of the antenna temperature of objects and background.

articleTitle: Data association of monostatic-bistatic composite HF radar network under ionospheric interference
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: High Frequency Surface Wave Radar (HFSWR) is superior to detect and track beyond-the-horizon targets but susceptible to the ionosphere interference because of the specific wavelength. Seeking out the real target points from plenty of false ones is an obsessional problem for data association. This is commendably solved by establishing a new radar system, the monostatic-bistatic composite radar network, and providing a novel process data association with steps of space cursory association, time cursory association, etc. The validity of this method is substantiated by the simulation results.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Square Slot Antenna with Parasitic Patch
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized square slot microstrip antenna with parasitic patch is presented. In this study, the antenna is excited by L-shaped microstrip feed line. The wide axial-radio (AR) and impedance bandwidth are achieved by adjusting the parasitic patch and relative parameters. The proposed antenna has been optimized and fabricated, and the measured results demonstrate a 3-dB AR and 10 dB return loss with bandwidth around 44.9% and 44.4% respectively.

articleTitle: The simulation and analysis of the interference from ultra-wideband system to spread spectrum communication system
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Ultra wideband (UWB) system operates by transmitting signals over a very wide band of spectrum, so there must be the problem of coexistence of UWB with other radio services besides the spread spectrum communication system. By designing the simulation models of UWB system and spread spectrum system which is used more broadly, the simulation experiments has been taken on the performance of spread spectrum under the interference from UWB. The results prove the validity of simulation model. And the main factors are analyzed on UWB interference to the spread spectrum communication, and the corresponding results are given.

articleTitle: PSO algorithm for amending the “minus beam” pointing error after phase defocusing
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The ldquominus beamrdquo steering of the phased arrays deviates from the given direction because of the quantization phase in the digital phased shifter. This paper studied the theory of wide-beam and ldquominus beamrdquo and investigated the model of the particle swarm optimization method on the arrayspsila beam steering, and modified the range of the position and speed factor by the principle of random phase quantization. The simulating results show the effectiveness and correctness of the method.

articleTitle: Flexible compact planar inverted-F antenna for GSM/DCS/PCS triple-band applications
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A compact design of a flexible planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) is proposed for triple-band (GSM/DCS/PCS) mobile phone applications. The main radiating element of the antenna, which generates the GSM and DCS resonant modes, is printed on a flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) and rolled in a form of cylinder. To enhance the bandwidth of the high band, a metallic rod working as a parasitic element of the antenna is introduced into the antenna design. The antenna prototype was fabricated and measured. Good agreement between the measurement and simulation results can be achieved.

articleTitle: Study on time-sharing methods for hardware-in-the-loop radar netting simulation
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Two time-sharing simulation methods are proposed, which solve the problem of adopting one set of hardware - in - the- loop(HITL) radar to simulate radar netting. First, an applied HITL system is introduced. Then the flows for the two methods are described, and the key process of the methods - data association and fusion algorithms are presented. Finally the advantages and disadvantages of the two methods are discussed and some valuable conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: A printed dipole array for omni directional application
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Design and measured results of printed dipole array conformed around a conducting cylinder with 0.13λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> spacer in between are described. The dipoles in array are identical, with spacing d (0.51 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and in circumferential direction. Corporate feed network is used to ensure the dipole radiating element’s uniform amplitude and phase. It has omni directional radiation pattern coverage around the cylinder. This structure allows for large bandwidth (SWR of less than 2 over the bandwidth in excess of 21 percent). The results obtained show that as the number of array’s dipole radiating elements increased, the radiation hole at the cylinder axial direction will gets narrower.

articleTitle: A New Method of Camouflage Jamming against ISAR Based on Compensating Modulation
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: It is quite significant in the military field that an effective jamming can be executed against inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) successfully. However, ISAR has a well anti-jamming capability, which is stronger than that of conventional radar due to its special imaging approach. Camouflage jamming with many particular advantages becomes a very effective and important jamming approach nowadays. However, it is a novel and important technologic approach that an effective camouflage jamming can be carried out against ISAR. A new method of camouflage jamming is proposed in the paper, based on principle of ISAR imaging. The compensating modulation can be employed for the ISAR signals received by jamming device to achieve camouflage jamming, based on the phase relationship between ISAR signals received by jamming device and the real returned signals of targets. The feasibility and effectiveness of the methods are verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Fast analysis of wideband electromagnetic scattering from multi-objects based on characteristic basis function method
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: The asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) is an efficient method for analyzing wideband electromagnetic scattering problems. As the number of unknowns increases, the size of MOM impedance matrix grows very rapidly, so it is a prohibitive task for the computation of wideband radar cross section (RCS) from electrically large objects or multi-objects using the traditional AWE technique. The characteristic basis function method (CBFM) is a novel efficient approach for reducing the matrix size to a manageable size for direct matrix inversion. In this paper, the AWE technique based on the CBFM for analyzing electromagnetic scattering from multi-objects over a given frequency band is proposed. Numerical examples are given to illustrate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Novel Compact Power Divider with Harmonic Suppression for Phased Array Antenna Application
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This paper presents a novel compact power divider with third harmonic suppression and also can provide a direct current (dc) path which could simplify the other active circuits, such as power amplifier, in the complicated phase array antenna feeding network area. The proposed power divider achieves 20% size reduction compared to the conventional Wilkinson power divider and it is beneficial to the miniaturisation of the phased array antenna. From the measured results, it can be seen that the simulated results can instruct the practical circuit very well.

articleTitle: Design of the UWB antenna using fractal concept
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: In this paper a novel barbell-shaped planar antenna for UWB application is proposed. The antenna, composed of two symmetrical fractal patch radiators and partially grounded plane which are used to realize the characteristic of ultra-wideband (UWB), can occupy about 3.95 GHz bandwidth (from 3.45 GHz to 7.40 GHz), which is equivalent to 73%. The symmetrical radiation patterns in the y-z and x-z planes are obtained for the potential of pattern reconfigurable. An optimized UWB antenna is designed and simulated by ansoft-HFSS.

articleTitle: Estimate of shielding efficiency for double layer enclosure with apertures array
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: A relatively simple Transmission Line Model (TLM) has been developed to research the coupling efficiency (CE) characteristic of electromagnetic pulse and the shielding efficiency (SE) of double layer shielding rectangular enclosure with apertures. The electric coupling efficiency (CE) of single layer with aperture is compared with that of double layer with apertures array. The simulation results show that: SE can be improved greatly with double layer shielding and it is worse on the resonance frequency of enclosure modes. On the condition of enclosure resonance, SE drops significantly in the centre of inner enclosure. The finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) result is used to compare the results of TLM. Further discuss shows that the coupling efficiency decreases by the increasing number of apertures when the total area of apertures is kept the same.

articleTitle: Experiment study about coupling effect of single-chip system under different electromagnetic pulse
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: This work mainly aims at the study of experiment about coupling effects of single-chip system under electromagnetic pulse (EMP). The results show that the coupling degree of the connected lines to the pulse field and the characters of the EMP have notable influences on the interference peak value.

articleTitle: Design of a high gain microstrip antenna array at Ku-band
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
abstract: Aperture coupling feed and double-layer microstrip patch structure are applied to design microstrip antenna element, 64 elements and 256 elements microstrip antenna array. Parallel feed and T-junction type power divider are used to design antenna array. The measured results of subarray antennas show that the operational bandwidth (VSWR ≤ 1.5) is 1.32GHz and the gain is not less than 24dB which is accorded with the simulated results. The measured radiation patterns of 64 elements and 256 elements antenna arrays are presented.

articleTitle: Typical channel coding and modulation scheme for satellite communication systems
publicationTitle: 2008 8th International Symposium on Antennas, Propagation and EM Theory
